building-documentation.html.title: Building and maintaining documentation | AstroView documentation
building-documentation.html.summary: Building and maintaining documentation AstroView has two documentation sets: the Core developer guide and the desktop user manual. Markdown sources remain readable in GitHub. A pinned local DocFX tool builds a searchable HTML edition and generates the complete public Core API reference from the compiled assembly and its XML comments. Build and preview Prerequisites: .NET 10 SDK and PowerShell (PowerShell 7 on Linux/macOS). Python 3.10+ is used for snippet/site verification in CI. The HTML/API generator itself does not require Python or Node.js. From the repository root: ./eng/Build-Documentation.ps1 On Windows PowerShell with local script execution disabled, invoke the script with a process-local execution policy: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/Build-Documentation.ps1 Output is artifacts/documentation/site/index.html. To preview with navigation and search over HTTP: ./eng/Build-Documentation.ps1 -Serve Open http://localhost:8080 and stop the local server with Ctrl+C. The server is bound to localhost. Serving over HTTP is recommended because browser restrictions on local file: URLs can interfere with search and navigation requests. CI uploads the complete HTML edition as the documentation-site artifact. Download/extract it and serve that directory, for example with Python: python -m http.server 8080 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory path/to/extracted/site GitHub Pages publication The documentation is hosted at https://chuuei.github.io/AstroView-docs/. The source repository is private, and the account's current plan does not allow Pages on that repository. The public Chuuei/AstroView-docs repository contains only the generated site and its Pages deployment workflow. After a successful main-branch push CI run, refresh the hosted documentation: ./eng/Publish-Documentation.ps1 -RunId 123456789 Replace the number with the successful CI run ID. The command downloads its validated documentation-site artifact, checks its contents/links, and pushes only the generated site to the documentation repository. That repository's workflow deploys the update through GitHub Pages. Git and Python 3.10+ are needed; Git Credential Manager supplies the maintainer's existing GitHub credentials. No account credential is stored in the public repository or an Actions secret. The publisher rejects failed/non-main/non-push CI runs, expired artifacts, application/package binaries and scientific image files. build-info.json identifies the source commit and CI run. Local Git staging uses a fresh checkout under artifacts/pages-publication/; unrelated source changes are not published. Verify the deployed pages and exact source commit: python eng/documentation.py published --url https://chuuei.github.io/AstroView-docs/ --commit SOURCE_COMMIT_SHA The workflow template and documentation repository README are maintained in eng/pages/. Update them through the publisher rather than adding a private source-repository credential to a public deployment workflow. Structure Location Purpose docs/core/ Developer concepts, workflows, recipes and API map docs/desktop/ Installation, workspace procedures and troubleshooting docs/core/api/ Generated API YAML; ignored by Git and regenerated on build docs/images/ Branding and screenshots of the synthetic reference scene docs/template/ Small additions to DocFX's modern responsive/light/dark template docs/docfx.json, docs/**/toc.yml Content mappings and navigation dotnet-tools.json Pinned DocFX version and runtime roll-forward policy examples/AstroView.Core.Examples/ Compiled/runnable developer examples eng/documentation.py Snippet synchronization and built-site link checks The API input is AstroView.Core.dll and its side-by-side XML file in artifacts/documentation/core. Generating from the assembly avoids loading the desktop application into the API extractor and uses the actual built public API. DocFX documents supported public/protected visibility according to its default filter and includes explicit interface implementations. Keep examples correct Core guide code fences marked <!-- snippet: region-name --> are synchronized from named C# regions in the example program. Edit the C# first, then run: python eng/documentation.py sync python eng/documentation.py check dotnet run --project examples/AstroView.Core.Examples -c Release -- artifacts/documentation/examples The check command fails when displayed snippets drift from the compiled example. Examples create only their own small files and assert meaningful sample, checksum, signature, conversion or coordinate results. CI compiles the example project with the solution and runs it on Windows, Linux and macOS. Update a public API Update XML documentation in the Core source with the API change. Include units, coordinate conventions, ownership/lifetimes, defaults, precision constraints, parameters, return values and useful exceptions. Keep implementation internals out of the public contract. Do not edit generated API YAML/HTML. Update the relevant conceptual chapter and the support matrix when behavior changes. An API catalog entry does not by itself expand evaluated format support. Add or adapt a runnable recipe when it provides useful integration coverage. Update a desktop workflow Use the exact visible control labels, say which document/image the action uses, describe the expected result, and explain how to save the change. Keep developer implementation details in docs/desktop.md and the Core guide. Screenshots come from WorkspaceTests.DemoExercisesRealControlsAndEveryWorkspaceRenders. Run that test and copy workspace-0.png through workspace-7.png into the corresponding docs/images/desktop-*.png files when the UI changes. Inspect every image before committing it. Use only the synthetic reference scene: local user photographs and their test captures must remain excluded from published docs. Verification Documentation generation treats warnings as errors. After a build, run: python eng/documentation.py site --directory artifacts/documentation/site This validates generated local links, fragments, image resources, search data, manual entry points and API pages. It does not crawl external websites. The documentation CI job runs the same checks, while solution CI runs the executable examples on all supported platforms. Review the rendered desktop/mobile pages, search and representative API overload pages when changing navigation or styling.

core/api-reference.html.title: Core API reference guide | AstroView documentation
core/api-reference.html.summary: Core API reference guide The HTML documentation includes a generated reference for the public AstroView.Core API: types, constructors, overloads, signatures, generic constraints, properties, enum values, parameter descriptions, return values and declared exceptions. It is generated from the built Core assembly plus the same XML documentation distributed next to AstroView.Core.dll. In the HTML edition: browse the complete API namespace. Use the API navigation filter or site search for an exact type or member name. When reading on GitHub: use the type map below, the source tree, or build the HTML edition. Generated API pages are build output rather than checked-in copies of the implementation. Reading an API page Check whether the type represents parsed content, editable content or an operation/result. That distinction governs source lifetimes and fidelity. Choose an overload deliberately: paths, caller streams, parsed documents, editable documents and image sequences have different contracts. Read the default values in the signature and the XML remarks. In particular, sample layout, loss rejection, checksum generation and lazy access defaults affect integration behavior. Follow parameter/return-type links for option and result structures. Consult the conceptual guide for context; a type page cannot define your application's resource, identity-trust or fidelity policy. The catalog pages describe identifiers and types; the support matrix defines which associated conventions are evaluated, editable or preserved. Common entry points Operation Entry point Read an image document XisfReader.Load(...), FitsReader.Load(...) Get exact real samples XisfImage.GetSamples<T>(layout) Make editable XISF content XisfDocument.ToEditable() Preserve parsed XISF XisfWriter.Write(path, XisfDocument) Re-encode XISF XisfWriter.Write(path, XisfDocumentData, options) Render a preview XisfDisplayRenderer.Render(image, stretch) Validate supported semantics XisfDocument.Validate(), FITS diagnostics Verify signed XML XisfReader.VerifyXmlSignature(document) Convert with findings FitsConverter.ConvertToXisf(...), ConvertToFits(...) Create a native solution XisfAstrometricSolution.CreateLinear(...) API generation is part of documentation CI and uses warnings as errors. Update public XML comments with code changes; rebuild the reference rather than editing generated HTML/YAML. Follow documentation maintenance when adding types or recipes.

core/conversion.html.title: Converting FITS and XISF | AstroView documentation
core/conversion.html.summary: Converting FITS and XISF Preservation, transformation and omission Native document copying and cross-format conversion solve different problems. Use the native writer when retaining unknown extensions or format-specific structure matters. Use FitsConverter when you need a different image model, then inspect its findings before writing the destination. ConversionResult<T> contains Value, Findings and HasLosses. ConversionFinding exposes Code, Effect and Message. Effects distinguish preserved content, transformed content and omitted content. HasLosses tracks omissions; a transformation can still be scientifically important even when that Boolean is false. Read the findings rather than reducing them to one flag. Default loss policy The default policy is ConversionLossPolicy.Reject. A conversion with reported omissions throws ConversionLossException, which contains the findings. Use that exception to present a review step. Set Allow only when your application or user has accepted the omission policy. public static void Conversion(string directory) { var source = XisfReader.Load(Path.Combine(directory, "catalog.xisf")); try { _ = FitsConverter.ConvertToFits(source); // Rejects omissions by default. throw new InvalidOperationException("Expected metadata loss to require a decision."); } catch (ConversionLossException error) { foreach (var finding in error.Findings) Console.WriteLine($"{finding.Effect}: {finding.Code}: {finding.Message}"); } // Continue only after your application/user accepts the reported omissions. var accepted = FitsConverter.ConvertToFits(source, ConversionLossPolicy.Allow); FitsWriter.Write(Path.Combine(directory, "converted.fits"), accepted.Value); } Allowing omissions does not force an impossible pixel conversion. Unsupported complex image storage or an exactness constraint can still cause a failure. Do not catch every exception and retry with a lossy floating-point image unless that is a separately designed feature of your application. FITS to XISF ConvertToXisf(fitsDocument, options) returns editable images and findings. FitsConversionOptions.AxisInterpretation defaults to PreserveDimensions. Choose RgbOrRgba only for files whose third axis really represents color. IncludeStructuralKeywords controls whether structural FITS cards are also retained as XISF FITS keywords. FITS scaling/blank handling can transform stored integer data into physical floating-point samples. Conventional unsigned storage has dedicated typed paths. See FITS exact values before converting Int64 or UInt64 data through double precision. FITS table conversion can report omission of native table storage, units, scaling or extension details; array cells can be flattened to text. Unknown extensions may be omitted. Treat the result as a conversion of supported content, not a complete archive of the original FITS HDUs. XISF to FITS Prefer the XisfDocument conversion overload when reviewing an entire source document: it reports document-level as well as image-level omissions. Passing only selected image data cannot report content you have already left behind. Native XISF properties, astrometric solutions, global metadata, tables, color objects and application extensions may not have an equivalent FITS representation in this converter. Even if FITS has a related convention in principle, this implementation must explicitly support that mapping before it can preserve it. For selected-image export, first decide whether to retain or intentionally omit global properties and tables. Copying Images[0] into a new document does not automatically bring the original document's global content with it. Verify a conversion Review every omitted and transformed finding. Write to a new path with the chosen checksum policy. Reopen the output using your intended reader options. Compare dimensions, channel interpretation, sample types and values at the precision required by your application. Verify expected metadata and tables explicitly; pixel equality alone is not a document-fidelity check. Use independent readers/reference data for interoperability claims. The repository's interoperability evidence records independent tools, fixtures and remaining gaps. Self-generated examples and forward/backward conversions are useful regression checks but are not a substitute for independent validation.

core/coordinates.html.title: Coordinates and astronomy | AstroView documentation
core/coordinates.html.summary: Coordinates and astronomy FITS WCS and native XISF astrometry are separate models CelestialWorldCoordinateSystem.TryCreate accepts a FITS header or XISF FITS keywords. It supports recognized degree-based RA/Dec TAN WCS and supported legacy linear metadata without CTYPE. It does not evaluate every projection, frame, axis permutation or distortion convention found in a FITS header. Check the Boolean result before calling PixelToSky or SkyToPixel. A retained WCS card can be unsupported for evaluation. An unsupported model should produce an explicit unavailable-coordinate state in your application rather than falling back to an unrelated transform. XisfAstrometricSolution uses native AstrometricSolution: properties. It exposes an available layer and diagnostics, supports seven native projections and can evaluate supported projective/distortion layers. PCL/legacy property namespaces are not automatically relabeled as a native solution. Coordinate conventions API Image position convention Sky angles FITS PixelToSky / SkyToPixel Zero-based pixel centres; the API adapts FITS CRPIX RA/Dec in degrees Native XISF ImageToCelestial / CelestialToImage Pixel centres at half-integers: first pixel is (0.5, 0.5) RA/Dec in degrees Desktop Coordinates workspace Zero-based centres for both source models RA/Dec in degrees Do not add a FITS one-pixel offset before passing a zero-based position to PixelToSky. Do add the native half-pixel offset when adapting a zero-based pixel centre to the native XISF model. Conversely, subtract 0.5 from a native XISF image position when presenting zero-based pixel coordinates. Right ascension is an angle in degrees, not hours or an hh:mm:ss string. Convert an hour value by multiplying by 15 before calling these APIs. Declination must be within the model's supported angular domain. An inverse transform can throw when the sky position lies outside the projection's valid area. Create and check a native solution public static void Coordinates() { var solution = XisfAstrometricSolution.CreateLinear( "Gnomonic", [83.633, 22.0145], [512.5, 384.5], new double[,] { { -0.0003, 0 }, { 0, 0.0003 } }); // Native XISF pixel centres are half-integers: (0.5, 0.5) is the first pixel. var sky = solution.ImageToCelestial(512.5, 384.5); var pixel = solution.CelestialToImage(sky.RightAscension, sky.Declination); if (Math.Abs(pixel.X - 512.5) > 1e-6 || Math.Abs(pixel.Y - 384.5) > 1e-6) throw new InvalidOperationException("Astrometry round trip failed."); Console.WriteLine($"RA {sky.RightAscension}°, Dec {sky.Declination}°"); } Supported projection identifiers are Gnomonic, Stereographic, ZenithalEqualArea, Orthographic, PlateCarree, Mercator and HammerAitoff. The reference celestial coordinates and linear matrix use degrees and degrees per pixel. Matrix signs determine orientation; a negative horizontal term is common when right ascension increases toward the left. Use ApplyTo(editableImage) to write the solution's native properties. If a geometric operation changes an image in a way that cannot preserve its solution exactly, use RemoveFrom instead of retaining invalid astrometry. Display zoom and pan do not change image geometry; resampling/cropping in your own processing pipeline does. Work with loaded solutions Inspect image.AstrometricSolution, AvailableLayer and Diagnostics. A non-null object can carry metadata that is not fully evaluable. Do not infer availability solely from the presence of one property. Create validates a new property set more strictly; use it when constructing a complete solution. Test both the reference point and off-centre points. A forward/inverse round trip catches coordinate-convention mistakes but is not independent scientific validation: the same incorrect model can invert itself consistently. Use independent reference coordinates for accuracy-sensitive applications. Observation metadata AstronomyMetadata reads recognized XISF properties or FITS headers into AstronomyImageMetadata for values such as object, instrument, exposure and filter. Missing values remain optional. It does not perform plate solving, source detection, time-scale conversion or ephemeris computation. Consult the support matrix for the exact evaluated conventions.

core/data-model.html.title: Documents, pixels and ownership | AstroView documentation
core/data-model.html.summary: Documents, pixels and ownership Native documents and editable content Model Meaning Typical lifetime XisfDocument Parsed XML, images, properties, tables and source-aware blocks Retain its file/block sources until all required reads and saves finish XisfImage One parsed image, including its storage layout and scientific metadata May decode image or ancillary blocks lazily XisfDocumentData Editable document with images, global properties, creation metadata and tables Owned mutable state; avoid concurrent mutation XisfImageData Owned sample bytes plus editable image metadata Suitable for new images and re-encoding FitsDocument Ordered HDUs, diagnostics and materialized FITS payloads Independent of the input stream after loading FitsHdu Header, raw payload and optional decoded image/table interpretation Preserve the HDU to retain its native extension content Use XisfWriter.Write(path, parsedDocument) for document-preserving output. Use ToEditable() and the editable writer overload when you want to materialize content and choose new storage settings. The two overload families have different preservation behavior; see XISF. Dimensions and channels Dimensions are expressed as [width, height, further axes…]. Channel count is separate in the XISF model. The number of scalar samples is the product of the dimensions multiplied by the channel count; complex samples have two real components each. Validate products with checked arithmetic when allocating. FromArray(T[,]) follows CLR array indexing [height, width]. FromArray(T[,,]) follows [height, width, channel]. Do not copy the shape of a CLR array directly into the width-first dimensions argument. FITS axes describe scientific dimensions. A third axis of length three might be three wavelength planes rather than RGB. Conversion defaults to preserving dimensions; use FitsAxisInterpretation.RgbOrRgba only when that interpretation is appropriate for the data. Layout and endianness For two RGB pixels, planar sample order is R0 R1 G0 G1 B0 B1; interleaved order is R0 G0 B0 R1 G1 B1. Parsed and editable typed reads default to planar output even when the original file stores interleaved samples. Request the desired layout explicitly at application boundaries. ReadRawData() returns stored sample bytes after decompression and unshuffling. Those bytes still have the image's declared byte order and sample layout. IsBigEndian and PixelStorage describe how to interpret them. Typed methods perform byte-order handling for you. FITS raw image samples use FITS storage conventions; physical values additionally apply BSCALE, BZERO and BLANK. Numeric precision XISF image formats include UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Float32, Float64, Complex32 and Complex64. Property/table types include additional signed, vector, matrix and opaque representations; image and property type sets are not interchangeable. Access method Appropriate use Precision consequence GetSamples<ushort>(), GetSamples<ulong>(), etc. Real samples in a selected CLR representation Use a matching type for exact integer access; incompatible conversions can throw GetComplexSamples() Complex-valued scientific data Returns System.Numerics.Complex values; does not generate a magnitude/phase bitmap GetNormalizedSamples() Analysis relative to declared bounds Produces doubles and can round large integers; normalization is not display clamping FitsImage.GetPhysicalSamples() Convenient scaled physical values Produces doubles; not exact for all Int64/UInt64 values XisfDisplayRenderer.Render() Screen preview Produces 8-bit BGRA display pixels, not a scientific image conversion Every integer up to 2^53 is exactly representable in binary64; above that, some integers are not. Do not route UInt64 through double before formatting or serializing it. The exact-integer recipe demonstrates a typed FITS-to-XISF path for unsigned storage conventions. Ownership and concurrency Caller-provided streams remain open. XISF stream loads buffer input within the configured budget; path loads retain source information and may reopen files. Keep the original file and any referenced XISB files available and unchanged. Moving a header without its blocks can make a previously parsed document fail on a later pixel or metadata read. Parsed XML and exposed array values generally use detached copies. Modifying document.Xml alone does not update the document: use EditXml and retain its returned document. Typed sample arrays are new arrays. Editable metadata and table collections are mutable and are not a thread-safe shared editing model. Await asynchronous operations before mutating their inputs or releasing their sources. Async wrappers snapshot options, but that does not turn the entire editable object graph into an immutable snapshot. See resource policy and performance for memory and cancellation boundaries.

core/fits.html.title: Working with FITS | AstroView documentation
core/fits.html.summary: Working with FITS Documents, HDUs and headers FITS files are ordered sequences of header/data units (HDUs). Load a document with FitsReader.Load or its async overloads. Preserve the document's HDU order, including a primary HDU that may contain no image. document.Images is a convenience image sequence, not a replacement for the full HDU collection. FitsHdu.Content can expose a decoded FitsImage, FitsTable or no interpreted content. Unknown extensions can retain raw payloads. Header is an ordered collection of FitsHeaderCard records, so repeated cards and comments can be represented. Do not replace it with a dictionary if preservation matters. Use Set for a single-valued keyword and Add for repeated HISTORY or COMMENT records. FitsKnownKeywords and FitsKeywordKey<T> provide typed definitions for supported standard and convention-specific keywords. Create, write and verify an image public static void CreateFits(string directory) { ushort[] pixels = [0, 100, 200, 65535]; var image = FitsImage.FromPhysicalSamples(pixels, [2, 2]); var hdu = FitsHdu.CreateImage(image, primary: true); hdu.Header.Set("OBJECT", "M31"); hdu.Header.Add(new FitsHeaderCard("HISTORY", null, "Created with AstroView.Core")); string path = Path.Combine(directory, "image.fits"); FitsWriter.Write(path, new FitsDocument([hdu]), new() { WriteChecksums = true }); var loaded = FitsReader.Load(path); double[] physical = loaded.Images.First().GetPhysicalSamples(); if (!physical.SequenceEqual(pixels.Select(value => (double)value))) throw new InvalidOperationException("FITS sample round trip failed."); if (loaded.Hdus[0].ChecksumValid != true || loaded.Hdus[0].DataChecksumValid != true) throw new InvalidOperationException("FITS checksums failed."); } FromPhysicalSamples chooses appropriate FITS storage for supported input types, including conventional unsigned offsets. GetPhysicalSamples applies stored scaling and blank handling. Creating a primary image uses primary: true; additional image extensions use false after a valid primary HDU. FitsWriterOptions.WriteChecksums is false by default. Set it to true when you want the writer to generate CHECKSUM and DATASUM. After loading, checksum results are nullable: missing, valid and invalid are different states. Exact 64-bit values Physical double access can round large integer samples. For supported unsigned offset storage, use the typed conversion path and keep the result in ulong. public static void ExactIntegers() { ulong[] pixels = [0, 1, 9007199254740993UL, ulong.MaxValue]; var hdu = FitsHdu.CreateImage(FitsImage.FromPhysicalSamples(pixels, [2, 2]), primary: true); using var stream = new MemoryStream(); FitsWriter.Write(stream, new FitsDocument([hdu])); stream.Position = 0; var fits = FitsReader.Load(stream); var converted = FitsConverter.ConvertToXisf(fits); ulong[] exact = converted.Value[0].GetSamples<ulong>(); if (!exact.SequenceEqual(pixels)) throw new InvalidOperationException("Exact UInt64 conversion failed."); // GetPhysicalSamples() returns double and cannot retain all these integers. } This demonstrates a specific supported storage convention, not a promise that arbitrary Int64 FITS scaling can always be represented exactly in XISF. XISF has unsigned integer image formats, and signed/scaled FITS conversions can use a floating-point path or fail when exact representation is not available. Treat NotSupportedException as an explicit unsupported conversion. Structural edits Headers contain structural cards tied to payload geometry and storage, including BITPIX, NAXIS*, scaling and table layout cards. Editing such a card does not resize or reinterpret the payload safely. Use ReplaceImage to replace an image through the native model, or deliberately construct a new HDU. Core guards inconsistent structural edits when writing. Application code should offer a specific image-replacement operation rather than exposing every header card as an unrestricted text field. Use native document output to retain uninterpreted extensions; conversion is a separate, potentially lossy operation. FITS tables Parsed ASCII and binary tables expose Columns and Rows. Column metadata includes format, units, scale, zero point and null conventions. Values can be arrays or exact integer types, so avoid stringifying every cell if subsequent computation or round-trip fidelity matters. The native table model is read-only. Preserve the containing HDU when retaining original table storage. Conversion to XISF can transform tables and report loss of original storage/extension details; it is not a native FITS table editor. See metadata and tables. Validation and unsupported conventions FitsValidationMode.Tolerant records supported conformance findings and is the default. Strict rejects error-level findings. Neither mode enables a missing codec or convention. Image decompression for tiled/compressed FITS and broader WCS evaluation remain roadmap items. Retaining a header containing SIP, TPV or another WCS convention does not make that convention evaluable by CelestialWorldCoordinateSystem. Always check TryCreate before using a coordinate transform. Consult coordinates, reader budgets and the support matrix for supported operations and limits.

core/getting-started.html.title: Installation and quick start | AstroView documentation
core/getting-started.html.summary: Installation and quick start Requirements Use a .NET 10 SDK to build an application against AstroView.Core. The library itself needs .NET 10 at runtime. It has no graphical subsystem requirement. Nullable reference types and implicit usings are enabled in the sample project. Choose one of the following consumption methods. Use the actual version from your release or locally built package rather than assuming that a version has already been published to nuget.org. Method Setup Dependency handling Project reference Reference src/AstroView.Core/AstroView.Core.csproj from another project Normal NuGet restore of Core's dependencies Local NuGet source Extract the Core release; add its nuget directory as a package source NuGet restores the compression and cryptography packages Direct DLL reference Extract the complete Core ZIP; import AstroView.Core.props The import references and copies the supplied DLLs For a local package source: dotnet new console --framework net10.0 --name MyAstroTool dotnet nuget add source /absolute/path/to/extracted/nuget --name AstroViewLocal dotnet add MyAstroTool package AstroView.Core --version 0.2.0 Replace 0.2.0 with the package's version, including its prerelease suffix if present. Keep nuget.org enabled so package dependencies can restore. For the direct DLL method, add this after your target framework property group: <Import Project="path/to/extracted/AstroView.Core.props" /> Retain the archive's directory structure. The reference file selects the proper cryptography implementation for the target, including cross-publishing. Avoid mixing these direct references with different versions of the same NuGet dependencies. See the Core archive README and release guide. Create an image The recipe below uses using AstroView.Core;. Its directory argument is a writable output directory created by the caller. Dimensions are width then height; one channel means a monochrome image. FromSamples copies the input. public static void CreateXisf(string directory) { ushort[] pixels = [0, 100, 200, 65535]; var image = XisfImageData.FromSamples(pixels, [2, 2], 1); image.Id = "Luminance"; image.Properties.Set(XisfKnownProperties.Observation.Object.Name, "M31"); image.FitsKeywords.Add(XisfFitsKeyword.FromValue("EXPTIME", 180.0, "Seconds")); XisfWriter.Write(Path.Combine(directory, "image.xisf"), [image], new() { Compression = XisfCompression.Zstd, Shuffle = true, Checksum = XisfChecksum.Sha256 }); } This creates a 2 × 2 UInt16 XISF image with Zstandard compression, byte shuffle, a SHA-256 block digest, an object name and an exposure keyword. Read it back public static void ReadXisf(string directory) { var document = XisfReader.Load(Path.Combine(directory, "image.xisf")); var image = document.Images[0]; ushort[] pixels = image.GetSamples<ushort>(); Console.WriteLine($"{image.Dimensions[0]} × {image.Dimensions[1]}, {image.ChannelCount} channel(s)"); if (!pixels.SequenceEqual(new ushort[] { 0, 100, 200, 65535 })) throw new InvalidOperationException("XISF sample round trip failed."); } Load parses the document. GetSamples<ushort>() forces the selected image's data to decode and verifies any declared block checksum. The returned array is owned by your application. Mutating it does not update the parsed image. Run all examples From the repository root: dotnet run --project examples/AstroView.Core.Examples -c Release -- artifacts/my-examples The executable creates its own small FITS/XISF files and checks the results. It does not require downloaded astronomical photographs. Subsequent runs reuse the chosen output directory, so choose a dedicated example directory. Next, read documents, pixels and ownership before integrating large files or editable documents into a long-lived application.

core/imaging-analysis.html.title: Rendering and analysis | AstroView documentation
core/imaging-analysis.html.summary: Rendering and analysis Scientific samples, display pixels and measurements serve different purposes. Choose the representation deliberately and preserve the original scientific samples when producing a preview. Render a display image XisfDisplayRenderer.Render accepts a parsed or editable image. It returns an XisfBgra32Image: dimensions, DPI and owned BGRA pixels with straight alpha. The output is suitable for a graphics adapter but is not an encoded PNG/JPEG. Choose an image encoder in your application if you need a preview file. Stretch argument Behavior null Linear normalization for display XisfStretchOptions.Auto Adaptive display stretch with linked channels by default XisfStretchOptions.DisplayFunction Uses a stored display function where applicable New XisfStretchOptions Configure target background, shadow clipping, channel linking and stored-function use The Core automatic stretch defaults to target background 0.25 and shadow clipping -2.8. The desktop chooses 0.22 for its initial preview. Do not assume that every caller uses the same application-level defaults. The renderer supports supported two-dimensional real images and interprets orientation, relevant color metadata and alpha. Complex magnitude/phase display and a general scientific cube-plane renderer are not implemented. Read those samples through the scientific APIs instead. Statistics, histogram and region example public static void AnalyzeAndRender(string directory) { var image = XisfReader.Load(Path.Combine(directory, "image.xisf")).Images[0]; var statistics = image.CalculateStatistics(new() { Normalize = false, MaximumSamplesPerChannel = 100_000 }); var histogram = image.CalculateHistogram(channel: 0, binCount: 256, lowerBound: 0, upperBound: 65535); ushort[] region = image.ReadRegion<ushort>(0, 0, 2, 1); var preview = XisfDisplayRenderer.Render(image, XisfStretchOptions.Auto); Console.WriteLine($"Mean: {statistics[0].Mean}; preview: {preview.Width} × {preview.Height}"); if (histogram.Bins.Sum() != 4 || !region.SequenceEqual(new ushort[] { 0, 100 })) throw new InvalidOperationException("Analysis example failed."); // preview.Pixels is BGRA32 display data. It is not a PNG file. } ReadRegion<T> returns all image channels in the requested layout. To read a whole channel, use ReadChannel<T>(channel). Region coordinates are zero-based; width and height must be positive and remain within a two-dimensional image. The region method still decodes the complete source block before extracting the requested rectangle. Interpret measurements correctly CalculateStatistics returns one XisfChannelStatistics per channel. It exposes sampled count, finite/non-finite counts, extrema, mean, standard deviation, median and median absolute deviation (MAD). MaximumSamplesPerChannel defaults to 1,000,000 in Core. Sampling can miss an isolated extreme or rare invalid value; these statistics are not guaranteed full-image extrema when sampling occurs. Normalize = true expresses measurements relative to declared image bounds. It is independent of display stretching. Values outside declared bounds can remain outside the normalized interval rather than being silently clamped. Median/MAD and other measurements use floating-point representations, so very large integer values can round. Histograms examine every sample in one chosen channel. The result separates in-range bin counts, underflow, overflow and non-finite counts. A histogram's bin sum alone is not necessarily the total number of pixels: include the other counts when checking totals. Bounds use scientific values, not automatically the units shown in a normalized statistics table or stretched preview. Do not derive a scientific histogram from 8-bit preview pixels. That would measure the display transformation rather than the source image. Color and display utilities XisfColorSpace provides RGB ↔ XYZ, RGB ↔ Lab and grayscale/luminance operations. Its default working space is D50-adapted sRGB. XisfDisplayFunctions contains display/midtones utilities. Specify a supported working space when a file's metadata requires a different interpretation. These transforms are not a full ICC engine, an image calibration workflow or a general photometry package. AstronomyMetadata and coordinate models provide specific metadata/astrometry support; broader astronomical algorithms should be documented separately as they are added. Memory and UI integration A BGRA preview requires roughly four bytes per output pixel in addition to source/decompressed data. Typed reads allocate arrays; normalization adds double buffers. Avoid retaining several previews and sample copies for every open large document. Perform expensive rendering and analysis away from your UI thread, then transfer owned output to your UI framework. Read resource policy and performance for practical limits.

core/index.html.title: AstroView.Core developer guide | AstroView documentation
core/index.html.summary: AstroView.Core developer guide AstroView.Core is a .NET 10 library for astronomical image files. It contains FITS and XISF readers and writers, native document models, typed metadata and tables, scientific sample access, display rendering, statistics, conversion, validation and supported astrometric transforms. All public APIs use the AstroView.Core namespace, including types stored in the Fits, Xisf, Imaging and Astronomy source directories. The library is independent of Avalonia and the AstroView desktop application. Compression and XML cryptography have managed package dependencies, distributed with the Core release or restored through NuGet. No XISFLib package is required. Choose the appropriate operation Your task API family Guide Inspect an existing XISF/XISH header or image XisfReader, XisfDocument, XisfImage XISF Create or re-encode XISF XisfImageData, XisfDocumentData, XisfWriter XISF Read or preserve FITS HDUs FitsReader, FitsDocument, FitsHdu, FitsWriter FITS Work with exact pixels and channel layout Typed sample methods and XisfImageExtensions Data model Add properties, keywords or a catalog Property collections, known keys, table models Metadata and tables Produce a preview or measurements XisfDisplayRenderer, statistics and histograms Rendering and analysis Transform image and sky coordinates CelestialWorldCoordinateSystem, XisfAstrometricSolution Coordinates Assess integrity and conformance Validators, digest checks, XML signatures Validation Move between FITS and XISF FitsConverter, ConversionResult<T> Conversion Integration principles Decide whether you need document preservation, editable content or a cross-format conversion. They have different fidelity contracts. Keep file sources available while a parsed XISF document can still read lazy blocks. Loading its XML does not materialize every image or ancillary block. Use a sample type that preserves the values you need. A double array is convenient for analysis but cannot represent every 64-bit integer. Configure budgets and external-resource policy before accepting arbitrary files. Reuse a deliberate policy across reads rather than raising limits in response to each failure. Treat preview pixels, scientific samples, file digests, semantic validation and signer trust as separate concepts in your application. Version and support contract The examples target .NET 10 and the 0.2.0 API. Local builds have a -dev suffix; CI and tagged versions follow the versioning policy. A project targeting an older framework cannot reference the current library without being retargeted. Windows, Linux and macOS are exercised by CI. The support matrix distinguishes reading, writing, preservation and semantic evaluation for individual format features. Use that matrix when designing an import contract; the existence of an XML object or FITS card is not evidence that every associated convention is evaluated. Start with installation, or go directly to the API reference guide and executable recipes.

core/metadata-tables.html.title: Metadata and tables | AstroView documentation
core/metadata-tables.html.summary: Metadata and tables Property scopes XISF distinguishes document properties, image properties and creation metadata. XisfDocumentData.Properties contains global values; Images[i].Properties contains values for that image; Metadata contains XISF creation metadata. Creation identifiers must start with XISF:. Put application-defined data in your own property namespace instead of inventing creation keys. Property identifiers are case-sensitive. Known property definitions in XisfKnownProperties and XisfAdditionalProperties expose typed keys and provenance through MetadataDefinitionSource. Standardized identifiers and PixInsight/PCL conventions have distinct meanings and provenance; do not treat every catalog entry as part of the XISF standard. XisfPropertyCollection accepts supported CLR values, explicitly typed XisfPropertyData, or preserved parsed properties. Use a typed key where one is available. Explicit type information is useful for vector/matrix values and when an exact serialized type is part of an interchange contract. Create a document property and table public static void MetadataAndTables(string directory) { var loaded = XisfReader.Load(Path.Combine(directory, "image.xisf")); var editable = loaded.ToEditable(); editable.Properties["Example:Session"] = "Night 1"; editable.Images[0].Properties.Set(XisfKnownProperties.Observation.Object.Name, "M31"); var table = new XisfTableData { Id = "Stars", Caption = "Reference measurements" }; table.Fields.Add(new XisfTableFieldData("Name", "String")); table.Fields.Add(new XisfTableFieldData("Flux", "Float64")); table.Rows.Add(new object?[] { "Star A", 1234.5 }); editable.Tables.Add(table); string output = Path.Combine(directory, "catalog.xisf"); XisfWriter.Write(output, editable); if (XisfReader.Load(output).Tables.Count != 1) throw new InvalidOperationException("Table round trip failed."); } The example creates a document-level table. XisfImageData.Tables can instead attach tables to a particular image. Each row must match the field count, and cell CLR values must match their declared types. Numeric vectors and rectangular matrices are distinct from scalar cells. Use the API reference for field, row and cell models rather than relying on displayed table text. Parsed availability and opaque content Parsed XisfProperty and table-cell values can be unavailable while their XML remains preserved. Check IsAvailable and UnavailableReason before computing with the value. An absent property, an unavailable value and a value of zero are different states. Do not replace an unavailable value with zero or an empty string merely to simplify a UI. Array-valued parsed properties return owned copies. Changing an array returned by Value does not edit the original document. Use an editable collection or an explicit XML edit and retain its returned document. ToEditable() materializes images but can still retain source-aware opaque objects. Keep source blocks available through saving if opaque metadata is present. Choose the native parsed writer when preserving unfamiliar content is more important than changing the serialization strategy. FITS keywords FITS headers are ordered cards with case-insensitive keyword lookup. FITS cards stored inside XISF use XisfFitsKeyword, including text quoting conventions. XisfFitsKeyword.FromValue quotes and escapes strings correctly and handles commentary cards. Prefer it to building quoted text manually, particularly for object names containing apostrophes or slash characters. FITS keywords inside an XISF image are a metadata representation. They do not become native FITS HDUs until an explicit conversion. Conversely, an XISF property is not automatically representable as a FITS card. Conversion findings identify known omissions and transformations. Other metadata objects Object Core behavior Application implication Observation metadata AstronomyMetadata reads recognized fields into AstronomyImageMetadata Missing fields remain optional; units and interpretation matter Thumbnail Separate image object that can decode lazily Validate/decode it separately when verifying all payloads ICC profile Inspect/preserve profile bytes Core does not provide a complete ICC color-management engine CFA pattern Inspect/preserve mosaic metadata No debayering is implied Display function Stored display transformation Choosing it affects preview output, not source samples Native astrometry Parsed/evaluated where supported Validate availability and coordinate conventions before use Extension XML Preservable application-defined content Keep namespaces and referenced blocks intact For exact file-format coverage and remaining property/table corner cases, see the support matrix and interoperability evidence.

core/recipes.html.title: Executable recipes | AstroView documentation
core/recipes.html.summary: Executable recipes The examples in this guide come from one compiled C# program. Documentation CI checks that displayed snippets match that program, builds it against the current Core project and runs its round-trip checks on Windows, Linux and macOS. Run From the repository root with the .NET 10 SDK: dotnet restore AstroView.sln --locked-mode dotnet run --project examples/AstroView.Core.Examples -c Release -- artifacts/my-examples Use a dedicated writable directory. The program generates small artificial images; no external corpus, network access or GUI is required. It prints a success message only after every recipe completes. Recipe catalog Recipe Demonstrates Guide CreateXisf UInt16 creation, typed metadata, compression, shuffle and SHA-256 Quick start ReadXisf Lazy document access and exact typed sample reads Quick start CreateFits Primary image, ordered header cards and checksum verification FITS ExactIntegers UInt64 boundaries through supported FITS/XISF conversion FITS PreserveAndEdit XML edit and native document-preserving output XISF MetadataAndTables Global/image property scopes and a typed catalog Metadata and tables AnalyzeAndRender Statistics, full histogram, region access and BGRA preview Analysis Coordinates Native XISF coordinate conventions and inverse transform Coordinates Signatures RSA-signed copy, XML verification and pixel digest access Integrity Conversion Rejected omissions, findings and explicit loss opt-in Conversion ReaderLimits Resource policy, semantic diagnostics and block decoding Resources Distributed XISH header plus XISB blocks and relative resolution XISF AsyncIo Cancellation-aware async read/write lifetime Resources The source is in examples/AstroView.Core.Examples. All recipes use the same output directory; later recipes intentionally reopen files created earlier. They check expected values with normal C# exceptions, so they can also serve as a simple integration smoke test. These examples verify AstroView's own operations. For independently produced files and reference-reader comparisons, use the separate interoperability suite.

core/resources-performance.html.title: Resource policy and performance | AstroView documentation
core/resources-performance.html.summary: Resource policy and performance Understand the memory model first Current readers and operations are not a general streaming or memory-mapped processing API. FITS loads retain materialized HDU payloads. XISF path loads can defer blocks, but a pixel read/decompression materializes a complete block. Region extraction and sampled statistics do not make that block decode partial. For a 10,000 × 10,000 single-channel image, the pixel buffer alone is roughly 200 MB as UInt16, 400 MB as Float32 or 800 MB as double. RGB multiplies scientific sample storage by three; a BGRA preview adds roughly 400 MB. Compressed input, temporary codec buffers, typed copies, metadata and application state add more. Use these estimates for planning rather than interpreting them as peak-memory guarantees. XISF defaults Budget or policy Default Buffered input 1 GiB XML header bytes / XML characters 64 MiB / 64 × 1024² characters XML depth / elements 128 / 1,000,000 Images / dimensions per image 10,000 / 16 Pixels per image 2,000,000,000 Property count / table cell count 100,000 / 10,000,000 Decoded data block 1 GiB Decompression ratio 1000 Network timeout 30 seconds Network resources Disabled General external filesystem paths Disabled Header-relative data blocks Enabled Header-directory traversal Disabled Budgets protect different stages. Raising MaximumDataBlockSize does not raise every other limit or ensure sufficient memory. Some highly compressible but valid data can exceed the ratio limit; change a limit only with an understood workload. ExternalResourceResolver lets an application provide resource streams under its own policy. Treat URI authorization, credentials, allowed hosts/paths, timeouts and response-size enforcement as application responsibilities as well as honoring Core's access flags. A custom resolver is not permission to ignore the reader's resource policy. Resolver streams have the ownership contract documented on that API. FITS defaults Budget Default HDUs 1,024 Data bytes per HDU int.MaxValue Retained raw HDU payload total int.MaxValue bytes Header cards / padded header bytes per HDU 100,000 / 8 MiB Axes 32 Decoded table cells / scalar elements 10,000,000 / 10,000,000 per table Buffered input 1 GiB Validation mode Tolerant Table element budgets account for array elements, characters and bits, including repeated heap references. A small number of table cells can still expand into a large number of values. The total decoded byte setting describes retained raw HDU payloads; it is not a process-wide cap on every allocation. Async and cancellation public static async Task AsyncIo(string directory) { using var cancellation = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)); var document = await XisfReader.LoadAsync(Path.Combine(directory, "image.xisf"), cancellationToken: cancellation.Token); await XisfWriter.WriteAsync(Path.Combine(directory, "async-copy.xisf"), document, cancellationToken: cancellation.Token); // Await completion before changing editable objects or releasing source files. } The API includes worker-thread wrappers around synchronous parsing/codec work. Async does not imply incremental decoding, constant memory or cancellation inside every compression operation. Some work completes its current block before observing cancellation. Await completion before editing input objects or disposing streams your application supplied. Path writes stage single-file output and check cancellation around publication. Caller streams can contain partial data after errors/cancellation. Distributed XISF involves multiple paths and needs application-level cleanup/publication coordination. Practical integration choices Keep native documents and defer typed sample copies until needed. Request a matching integer type for exact work instead of normalizing every image to double immediately. Avoid repeatedly asking for the same full decoded block, typed copy and preview during a single operation. Cache owned results at your application layer when that tradeoff is appropriate, then release them when documents close. Bound concurrent decodes by available memory, not just processor count. Separate background work from UI updates and provide progress at meaningful operation boundaries rather than inventing per-pixel progress. Benchmark with your real sample types, channel counts, codecs and file layouts. A synthetic compression ratio or one codec benchmark does not predict all astronomical workloads. See testing for local corpus tests and the repository's performance tool. Broader streaming, shared typed access and compressed FITS are recorded in the roadmap.

core/validation-signatures.html.title: Validation, checksums and signatures | AstroView documentation
core/validation-signatures.html.summary: Validation, checksums and signatures Choose the question you need to answer Question Mechanism What it does not establish Can the header be parsed under my limits? Reader and reader options That every lazy block exists or decodes Is the supported structure semantically consistent? XISF/FITS diagnostics Complete implementation of every format convention Does XML satisfy a particular schema? XisfDocument.Validate(XmlSchemaSet) Valid pixels, cryptographic trust or a universal bundled schema Do stored blocks match their declared digests? Decode the XISF blocks Who produced the file Do FITS checksum cards verify? Nullable HDU checksum results Presence of checksum cards when the result is null Is signed XML intact for its embedded key? XisfReader.VerifyXmlSignature An authenticated signer identity Validate a loaded document public static void ReaderLimits(string directory) { var options = new XisfReaderOptions { MaximumDataBlockSize = 256 * 1024 * 1024, MaximumDecompressionRatio = 1000, AllowNetworkResources = false, AllowExternalFilePaths = false, AllowHeaderRelativeDataBlocks = true, AllowHeaderDirectoryTraversal = false }; var document = XisfReader.Load(Path.Combine(directory, "image.xisf"), options); var diagnostics = document.Validate(); foreach (var diagnostic in diagnostics) Console.WriteLine(diagnostic); _ = document.Images[0].ReadRawData(); // Forces the primary block to decode and check its digest. } Validate() returns diagnostics with severity, code, message and location. Loading and validating a header do not necessarily access all payloads. To check an entire XISF document, decode every primary image and available thumbnail and access any relevant ancillary blocks. Handle an unavailable optional object as a distinct result rather than discarding its preserved XML. For FITS, tolerant mode retains diagnostics; strict mode rejects error-level findings. Inspect both document diagnostics and ChecksumValid / DataChecksumValid on each HDU. Null means a corresponding checksum was absent, not that verification succeeded. Writers can generate checksums explicitly. Supply an XSD deliberately The library accepts a caller-created XmlSchemaSet. Select the XISF schema and revision appropriate to your interchange contract. When loading arbitrary schema files, disable DTD processing and external XML resolution unless your application deliberately supplies a trusted resolver. Schema validation and semantic validation complement each other; neither replaces payload decoding. Do not download schemas implicitly while opening an image in an offline tool. Ship or configure the trusted schema resources you require. The desktop XSD workflow uses a local caller-selected file and disables network/DTD resolution. Sign and verify a copy Use using System.Security.Cryptography; for this recipe. public static void Signatures(string directory) { var document = XisfReader.Load(Path.Combine(directory, "image.xisf")); using RSA key = RSA.Create(3072); string signedPath = Path.Combine(directory, "signed.xisf"); XisfWriter.WriteSigned(signedPath, document, key); var signed = XisfReader.Load(signedPath); if (!XisfReader.VerifyXmlSignature(signed)) throw new InvalidOperationException("XML signature verification failed."); // Decoding checks declared block digests too; signature verification alone does not decode all pixels. _ = signed.Images[0].GetSamples<ushort>(); } The example owns a temporary RSA key and disposes it when finished. A production application needs its own key storage, identity and trust policy. Verification against a key embedded in the document demonstrates internal integrity; anyone can generate a different key and sign a different document. Signing requires appropriate digests for attached/external data blocks. Do not strip block checksums before signing. Verification of signed XML is separate from reading all signed image data, so force the blocks to decode when your acceptance policy requires both checks. Changing signed metadata, image content or relevant serialization requires a fresh signature. Editable re-encoding drops the original signature; preserve the private key separately if you intend to sign new outputs with the same identity. Merely copying the old Signature element is not re-signing. Handle errors by category Category Typical exception/result Recommended application behavior Malformed or inconsistent format FitsFormatException, XisfFormatException Show the operation, file and diagnostic context Declared digest mismatch XisfChecksumException or FITS invalid checksum result Distinguish corruption from a missing digest Unsupported capability/type NotSupportedException Explain which operation is unavailable; retain native content if possible Rejected conversion loss ConversionLossException Present its findings and request an explicit loss decision Reader policy/budget failure Format, IO or policy exception with explanation Review limits/policy; do not silently retry with unlimited access Cancellation OperationCanceledException Treat as cancellation and release application-owned partial state Individual API pages describe their declared exceptions; this table is an integration guide rather than an exhaustive exception list. Logging a failed operation should not expose credential-bearing external resource URLs.

core/xisf.html.title: Working with XISF | AstroView documentation
core/xisf.html.summary: Working with XISF Open a document and inspect its contents Use XisfReader.Load(path, options) or LoadAsync for monolithic XISF files and distributed XISH headers. Stream overloads accept an optional base directory for resolving permitted relative blocks. Do not depend on a filename extension to establish the content's type in an application that accepts arbitrary input. A document can contain multiple images, document properties, creation metadata, document-level tables and application-defined extensions. Each image can also have properties, FITS keywords, tables, a thumbnail, an ICC profile, a CFA pattern, display functions and a working space. Inspect UnavailableObjects and property availability when an ancillary object is retained but cannot be interpreted. Header parsing and data decoding are separate operations. Selecting an image's typed samples can fail later because a block is missing, its checksum is wrong, its codec is unsupported or a resource budget would be exceeded. Choose preservation or re-encoding Goal Approach Consequence Copy a parsed document with its native content XisfWriter.Write(path, document) Preserves supported XML/opaque content and relocates its blocks as required Edit metadata while retaining source-aware content document.EditXml(...), then the parsed-document writer Original block references must remain meaningful until writing completes Change compression, storage placement or editable metadata document.ToEditable(), then editable writer plus options Materializes images; original signatures are not retained Create an image/document from scratch FromSamples, FromRaw, XisfDocumentData You are responsible for consistent dimensions, channels and metadata Document preservation does not mean byte-for-byte equality with the original file. Block offsets, header serialization and creation/storage details may differ. Preservation and interoperability are documented separately in the support matrix. Metadata-only preservation example Use using System.Xml.Linq; in addition to using AstroView.Core;. This example edits a new document-level property and writes a new file. public static void PreserveAndEdit(string directory) { var original = XisfReader.Load(Path.Combine(directory, "image.xisf")); var edited = original.EditXml(xml => { XNamespace ns = xml.Root!.Name.Namespace; xml.Root.Add(new XElement(ns + "Property", new XAttribute("id", "Example:Note"), new XAttribute("type", "String"), "Reviewed")); }); // The parsed-document overload preserves XML and opaque data blocks. string output = Path.Combine(directory, "preserved-copy.xisf"); XisfWriter.Write(output, edited); if (!XisfReader.Load(output).Images[0].GetSamples<ushort>() .SequenceEqual(original.Images[0].GetSamples<ushort>())) throw new InvalidOperationException("Preservation changed samples."); } Do not create duplicate property identifiers when applying the same edit to an already edited document. Locate and replace the existing element when that is the intended behavior. Changes to signed XML require a new signature. Writer settings Option Default Behavior Compression None None, Zlib, Lz4, Lz4Hc, Zstd Shuffle false Rearranges sample bytes before compression; decoding restores sample order Checksum Sha256 Also supports None, SHA-1, SHA-512 and platform-supported SHA-3 variants DataBlockStorage Attachment Attachment, Embedded or Inline text-block placement MaximumInlineBlockSize 65,535 bytes Larger text-encoded blocks fall back to attachment storage HexEncoding false Text blocks normally use Base64; enables hexadecimal instead CompressionSubblockSize 0 Zero disables splitting into independent compression subblocks BlockAlignmentSize 1 Alignment for attached blocks; 1 disables padding StringsAsDataBlocks false Nonempty String properties may be written as UTF-8 blocks CreatorApplication Core name/version Application attribution in creation metadata CreationTime Current UTC time Set explicitly for reproducible creation metadata These settings apply to writer overloads that serialize editable data or image sequences. The parsed-document overload has no re-encoding options parameter. Inline image samples use embedded Data elements where required by the format. SHA-3 availability depends on the platform cryptography implementation. Use a widely supported algorithm such as SHA-256 for a portable default and handle an explicit unsupported-algorithm failure rather than silently substituting a digest. Distributed output public static void Distributed(string directory) { var editable = XisfReader.Load(Path.Combine(directory, "image.xisf")).ToEditable(); string header = Path.Combine(directory, "distributed.xish"); string blocks = Path.Combine(directory, "distributed.xisb"); XisfWriter.WriteDistributed(header, blocks, editable, new() { Compression = XisfCompression.Lz4, Shuffle = true, Checksum = XisfChecksum.Sha256 }); if (XisfReader.Load(header).Images[0].GetSamples<ushort>()[3] != ushort.MaxValue) throw new InvalidOperationException("Distributed XISF round trip failed."); // Keep the header and its referenced block file together. } Distribute the header and every file it references together. The example uses relative sibling placement, which the default reader permits. A stream load needs an appropriate base directory to resolve those same paths. A distributed write publishes two paths and is not an atomic transaction. Applications should use a new output name, manage partial output cleanup and coordinate any final move themselves. Single-file path writers stage their output before replacing a destination; caller-owned streams can contain partial data after errors. See validation and signatures before claiming that a newly written document is fully verified.

desktop.html.title: Desktop development guide | AstroView documentation
desktop.html.summary: Desktop development guide For task-oriented application instructions, read the desktop user manual. This page covers development and the connection between workspaces and Core features. AstroView is an Avalonia 12.1 desktop application targeting .NET 10. Its scientific operations run through AstroView.Core; the library has no Avalonia dependency. The app starts with an original synthetic reference scene, so it works without downloads, internet access or the large local photograph corpus. dotnet restore AstroView.sln --locked-mode dotnet run --project src/AstroView.Desktop -c Release Open FITS, XISF or distributed XISH headers with Open images, drag files onto the window, or pass paths after -- on the command line. Detection reads the content rather than trusting extensions. The left sidebar selects documents and their image/HDU entries. Close documents to release retained pixels and previews. Workspaces Workspace What can be exercised Image Pan/zoom, fit and 1:1, orientation and alpha through Core, linear/adaptive/stored display functions, linked channels, target background, shadow clipping, observation metadata, explicit FITS RGB-axis interpretation, PNG display export. Inspect Search scoped FITS cards, creation/document/image properties and ancillary metadata; edit scalar metadata in memory; view formatted headers/XML; edit full XISF XML for advanced properties and extensions. Analyze Configurable sampled statistics (finite counts, extrema, mean, deviation, median, MAD), optional normalization, full-channel histograms, exact stored samples including UInt64/complex, and rectangular Float64 region inspection. Tables Native FITS ASCII/binary and XISF tables, exact integer text, array summaries, 200-row/16-column pages; create/replace XISF tables with typed scalar/vector/matrix JSON. Coordinates Supported FITS WCS and native XISF solutions, forward/inverse transforms, seven-projection synthetic calculator. All sky angles are degrees; displayed image coordinates use zero-based pixel centres. Integrity Semantic diagnostics, primary/thumbnail decoding with declared checksums, FITS CHECKSUM/DATASUM results, caller-supplied XSD, detached XML signature verification and signed-copy demonstration. Export Native document preservation, XISF re-encoding, FITS conversion, distributed XISF, fidelity reports and explicit loss opt-in; codecs, digests, shuffle, subblocks, alignment, text storage, hex/Base64 and string blocks. Isolate an image into a separate document when only that image is wanted. Feature lab Searchable capability guide, generated scientific images in all eight sample formats, both layouts and byte orders, RGB/XYZ/Lab/luminance/midtones calculator, reader budgets/policies and activity history. The reference scene contains synthetic Float32 RGB emission data, a UInt16 gradient, a scientific cube, a complex wave, a native linear astrometric solution, and a typed reference-star catalog. Generated data are demonstration data, not independent interoperability evidence and do not close AV-002's remaining gaps. The feature guide records the UI entry point and scope for each capability. Core features still on the roadmap are labelled unavailable. Complex and scientific cube samples remain inspectable; Core currently has no general magnitude/phase or cube-plane bitmap renderer. FITS table editing and broader WCS evaluation remain Core roadmap work. CFA and ICC metadata are inspectable/preservable; this does not imply debayering or a full ICC colour-management engine. Scientific values, editing and output Display stretching changes previews only. Histograms count all samples in one channel; statistics are estimates controlled by the sample limit. Their limits do not make the underlying full-image decoding a streaming operation. Large documents can retain substantial memory. Region access currently decodes full blocks. Integer statistics/Float64 region views can round very large integers; the stored-sample inspector prints UInt64 directly with exact integer text. Metadata and table edits apply to the in-memory document. Export a copy to persist them; active source filenames are guarded against replacement. Native copies use Core's document-preserving writer. Re-encoding materializes editable content and does not retain the original signature. Isolating an image copies its image metadata; document-level content stays in the original document. Conversion losses are rejected unless the user explicitly allows them. Inspect the fidelity report before accepting omissions; unrepresentable pixel types fail explicitly. Distributed output requires a new header name and creates a unique sibling block file. It is a two-file operation, not an atomic transaction; the app removes its new partial outputs on failure. The signed-copy demonstration generates an ephemeral RSA key, signs a copy and discards the private key. Embedded-key verification demonstrates integrity and does not authenticate an identity. The table JSON editor's example shows its schema. It supports scalar String, Boolean, TimePoint and the ordinary signed/unsigned integer and real types, plus integer/real vectors and rectangular matrices. It bounds interactive input to 1,000 rows, 32 fields and 4,096 elements per array cell. Core serializes the cells; the editor inserts embedded table XML without copying the original image blocks. Other types remain accessible through full XISF XML or the native Core API. Network resources, general external paths and directory traversal default off. Header-relative sibling blocks default on. Reader policy changes apply to newly opened documents. XSD loading disables DTD and network resolution. Long work runs off the UI thread; cancellation is cooperative and some codec/CPU operations finish their current block before returning. Publication operations disable cancellation in the UI while committing output. Keyboard and mouse Action Shortcut Open files Ctrl+O; Command+O on macOS Export document Ctrl+E Fit / 1:1 Ctrl+0 / Ctrl+1 Zoom / pan / fit Mouse wheel / left drag / double-click Select image pixel Click the image; coordinates adapt the stored orientation Cancel cooperative operation Escape or Cancel Development and verification dotnet build AstroView.sln -c Release --no-restore dotnet test AstroView.sln -c Release --no-build dotnet publish src/AstroView.Desktop -c Release --no-build -o artifacts/desktop-app The desktop workflow tests use Avalonia's headless platform with real Skia drawing and Inter fonts. They exercise native file loading, UI state, typed generation, metadata/table edits, exact samples, coordinates, validation, conversion loss rejection, re-encoding, distributed files, signatures and PNG output. Every workspace is rendered to tests/AstroView.Desktop.Tests/bin/Release/net10.0/ui-artifacts. Set ASTROVIEW_UI_ARTIFACTS to override that path. The headless dispatcher uses an explicit async result overload so tests await their complete workflow. CI runs both library and desktop tests on Windows, Linux and macOS. It uploads test results, the synthetic workspace screenshots and framework-dependent desktop publish directories. These builds require the .NET 10 runtime and the platform's ordinary Avalonia native prerequisites. Run dotnet AstroView.dll from a downloaded publish directory; no installer, signing/notarization or file association is supplied. Tagged GitHub releases provide a separate desktop ZIP with self-contained single-file executables. These include .NET and can run by themselves. Each is checked in isolation with --self-test before publication. The opt-in local desktop test renders the user's Bubble FITS and Carina Ha XISF files from C:\Code\AstroExamples, checks original hashes and keeps screenshots local under local-ui-artifacts in the test output. These photographs and captures are excluded from Git and CI uploads: dotnet test tests/AstroView.Desktop.Tests -c Release ` --environment ASTROVIEW_DESKTOP_EXAMPLES=C:/Code/AstroExamples ` --filter FullyQualifiedName~LocalDesktopTests Models adapt native documents for display; Services handle file dialogs, loading, table editing and export; ViewModels group operations by workspace; Views contain XAML; Controls draw the image viewport and histogram. Add a Core feature to the feature guide, its relevant workspace, a workflow test and this coverage table as it becomes available. Keep format/astronomy algorithms in Core. Avalonia's build-time telemetry can be disabled with AVALONIA_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 (already set in CI). Desktop dependency notices ship beside the app; they do not add GUI dependencies or GUI binaries to the Core NuGet.

desktop/analysis.html.title: Analysis and exact samples | AstroView documentation
desktop/analysis.html.summary: Analysis and exact samples Use Analyze to measure scientific sample values. A brightened preview can make faint structure easier to see, but it does not change the numbers measured here. Run statistics and a histogram Select the image in the sidebar. Open Analyze. Select the histogram Channel (zero-based). Choose Bins, Lower bound and Upper bound. Set Statistics sample limit and, if wanted, Normalize statistics to declared bounds. Click Run analysis. The statistics table contains all available image channels. The histogram shows the one channel chosen in the controls. For RGB, channels start at 0, 1 and 2; a fourth channel can be alpha where that is how the file represents it. Choose meaningful histogram bounds Use bounds appropriate to the source values. A normalized floating-point image might use 0 to 1; a full-range UInt16 gradient uses 0 to 65535. If you leave 0 to 1 for unnormalized UInt16 data, many values will appear as overflow instead of in the plotted bins. The application starts with 256 bins and accepts 8–4,096. More bins reveal finer distribution detail but do not increase the precision of the source image. The graph uses logarithmic counts to make small populations visible alongside large ones. The summary separates in-range, underflow, overflow and non-finite samples. Add all these counts when checking the number of samples in a channel; the bin sum alone can be smaller than the image's pixel count. Read the statistics table Column Meaning Ch Zero-based channel index Finite Number of sampled finite values Non-finite Sampled NaN/infinite values Min / Max Extrema among sampled finite values Mean Arithmetic average of sampled finite values Std dev Dispersion around the sampled mean Median Middle sampled value MAD Median absolute deviation, a measure of sampled spread The default statistics limit is 250,000 values per channel. The actual sample count can be smaller because the sampling stride is chosen to stay within that limit. Sampling can miss a rare hot pixel, non-finite value or extreme, so do not treat sampled Min/Max as guaranteed full-image bounds. Histograms inspect every sample in their selected channel. That is why their totals can differ from the sampled Finite/Non-finite counts. Raising the statistics limit improves coverage of the source but can increase processing time and memory. Normalization expresses statistics relative to declared bounds. It is independent of display stretch and does not automatically change the histogram's manually entered bounds. Floating-point statistics can round very large integers; use the exact sample inspector when integer precision matters. Inspect exact stored samples Scroll to SAMPLE INSPECTOR → Exact stored samples. Enter a zero-based linear start index and a count from 1 to 256, then click Read. The range must fit in the image buffer. The index is a linear storage index, not an (x,y) position. In planar data, one channel's samples precede the next channel's samples; in interleaved data, channels alternate within each pixel. Consult the selected image's metadata for layout and sample type. FITS data is presented through the application's supported image interpretation, including its scaling conventions. UInt64 values are printed directly as integer text rather than passing through double precision. For a useful demonstration, generate a UInt64 image in Feature lab → Image generator and read its first four samples. You should see 0, 1, 9007199254740993 and 18446744073709551615. Complex data can be inspected here even though it has no general image preview. The display keeps its real/imaginary sample representation available rather than pretending it is an ordinary monochrome exposure. Read a rectangular region In Rectangular region, enter zero-based X/Y and positive width/height, then click Read. The selected histogram channel determines which channel is shown. The rectangle must stay inside a two-dimensional image. Region values are displayed as Float64, so very large integers may round. Widths/heights are bounded by the controls, and the interactive inspector limits the total region samples, including all channels, to 4,096. A smaller displayed region still requires decoding the full source block; this is not an on-disk partial-read feature. Reduce the region when the limit is exceeded, and use exact stored samples for UInt64 precision checks.

desktop/coordinates.html.title: Image and sky coordinates | AstroView documentation
desktop/coordinates.html.summary: Image and sky coordinates The Coordinates workspace transforms positions using a supported astrometric solution stored with the selected image. It also contains a separate projection calculator for experimentation. Check the solution first Read ASTROMETRIC SOLUTION before calculating. A supported native XISF solution is used when available; otherwise the application can use recognized FITS WCS metadata. The reference emission nebula provides a native Gnomonic solution for this exercise. A file can contain astrometry-related properties that the current implementation cannot evaluate. Preserved WCS metadata is still visible in Inspect, but it is not automatically an available coordinate model. AstroView does not plate-solve an unsolved image when you open this workspace. Pixel to sky Select the desired image. Enter Image column / row under PIXEL → SKY. Click Calculate sky coordinates. Read right ascension (RA), declination (Dec) and the input image position in the RESULT area. Image positions are zero-based pixel centres in this workspace: (0,0) is the first pixel centre. You can also click a pixel in the Image workspace to select a position, then switch to Coordinates. The application adapts FITS reference pixels and native XISF half-integer centres internally. Sky to pixel Enter Right ascension / declination (°) under SKY → PIXEL. Click Calculate image coordinates. Read the zero-based column and row in the result. Enter both angles in degrees. RA expressed in hours must first be multiplied by 15; 5.5 hours is 82.5 degrees. Do not type an hh:mm:ss string into a numeric degree field. A resulting position outside the image is not necessarily an error: that sky location may be outside the recorded field. Positions outside the projection's mathematical domain can instead produce an explicit error. To practice, use the reference nebula, enter column 512 and row 384, calculate sky coordinates, then calculate image coordinates from the resulting RA/Dec. You should return close to the original position within numeric precision. Projection lab The PROJECTION LAB uses a separate synthetic model. It never changes your document's astrometry. Enter a reference RA/Dec in the sky-coordinate fields. Enter the image column/row you want to test. Choose one of the seven projection names. Click Evaluate forward + inverse. Read the synthetic sky position and inverse image position in the result. Available projections are Gnomonic, Stereographic, ZenithalEqualArea, Orthographic, PlateCarree, Mercator and HammerAitoff. The synthetic model uses image reference (512.5,384.5) in native XISF coordinates and a 0.0003°/pixel scale, with a negative horizontal matrix term. The workspace continues to present zero-based positions to you. Different projections have different valid areas and behavior near poles or boundaries. An error in the lab can indicate an invalid projection-domain position rather than a problem with your input file. Current support boundary FITS evaluation includes recognized RA/Dec TAN and supported legacy linear metadata; broader FITS projections/distortion conventions remain limited. Native XISF evaluation supports its implemented solution layers and seven projections. The lab's seven projections do not expand FITS WCS support. See limits if a solution remains unavailable, and keep the original metadata when exporting a native copy.
