desktop/export.html.title: Export and conversion | AstroView documentation
desktop/export.html.summary: Export and conversion The Export workspace saves scientific documents. Use Image → Export preview as PNG… for a rendered picture instead. Choose an output operation Output choice Use it for What to review Keep native document Save the current native FITS/XISF document and its in-memory edits Retains the native document model; does not apply new XISF compression settings Re-encode as XISF Write XISF with the chosen storage/compression settings; convert supported FITS content if needed Materializes content; re-encoding and native preservation have different metadata/signature guarantees Convert to FITS Write a FITS document from supported XISF content, or write an already native FITS document Review XISF-specific content that cannot be mapped Distributed XISF (XISH + XISB) Write a new header plus a sibling data-block file Keep both files together; requires a new header filename The output applies to the whole selected document, not just the image you are looking at. To export a single image, use the isolation procedure below. Save a native copy Finish any metadata/table/XML edits. Choose Keep native document. For FITS output, leave Write FITS CHECKSUM / DATASUM selected if you want new checksum cards generated. Click Export document…. Choose a new filename and location. Reopen the output and inspect/validate the saved result. AstroView guards the active source filenames against replacement. Use a new output path rather than trying to overwrite an open source. Native preservation does not promise that serialized file bytes or offsets are identical to the original; it preserves the supported native document content. Convert with a fidelity review Select the required destination choice. Click Analyze fidelity. Read each Effect, Code and Finding in PRESERVATION REPORT. If omissions are listed, decide whether the resulting document is suitable for your work. Select Allow reported conversion losses only if you accept those omissions. Export to a new path, reopen it and validate/check expected content. The default rejects reported losses. This protects properties, global metadata, tables, color/astrometry objects or extension content that the converter cannot represent. An allowed loss does not make an unsupported pixel conversion possible; complex images, for example, cannot be written as ordinary FITS image HDUs by this converter. An empty report can mean no cross-format conversion is required. It does not make re-encoding equivalent to native preservation. Read the operation description and check signatures/advanced metadata as appropriate. Re-encode XISF Choose Re-encode as XISF, then scroll through XISF RE-ENCODING. These controls apply to XISF re-encoding and distributed output, not to a native copy or native FITS writer. Setting Meaning Compression Uncompressed, zlib, LZ4, LZ4 high compression or Zstandard Byte shuffle Rearranges sample bytes for compression; reading restores them Block digest No digest, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA3-256 or SHA3-512 Block placement Attached binary blocks, embedded text blocks or inline text blocks Hex instead of Base64 Changes the text encoding used for text blocks Store strings as data blocks Uses UTF-8 blocks for nonempty string properties Alignment (bytes) Padding/alignment for attached blocks; 1 disables alignment padding Inline limit (bytes) Threshold for text-encoded blocks; larger blocks can use attachments Compression subblock bytes Splits compression into independent subblocks; 0 disables splitting The desktop initially selects Zstandard, byte shuffle, SHA-256, attached blocks, 4096-byte alignment, a 65535-byte inline limit and no subblock splitting. These are application defaults, not mandatory settings for every XISF file. The listed compression codecs are lossless for stored sample bytes; they do not turn a Float32 image into an 8-bit picture. File size and encoding speed depend on the actual data. Text encoding and alignment can add size even when a codec compresses the payload well. SHA-3 support depends on platform cryptography; if an algorithm is unavailable, select a supported digest such as the default SHA-256 and review the error rather than assuming it was substituted. Re-encoding materializes image data and drops the previous signature. If a new signature is wanted, sign the output copy afterward. Some opaque content can still depend on source blocks, so keep source files available until saving finishes. Export just one image Select the desired image. Click Isolate selected image as a new document. Select the newly created document in the sidebar. Inspect its metadata, then choose the output operation and export. Image metadata is copied with the isolated image. Global document properties, document-level tables and other global content stay in the original document. Decide whether that is appropriate before using the isolated output as an archive of an observation. Write a distributed document Choose Distributed XISF (XISH + XISB) and a new .xish output name. The app creates a uniquely named sibling block file and writes its reference in the header. Keep both files together when moving or sharing the result. This is a two-file operation rather than one atomic file replacement. The app cleans up its new partial outputs after a failure where possible. Reopen the header and validate it after saving. Sending the header alone is not sending the image pixels.

desktop/feature-lab.html.title: Feature lab and reader settings | AstroView documentation
desktop/feature-lab.html.summary: Feature lab and reader settings Feature lab contains a capability guide, a scientific image generator, a color calculator, reader-policy settings and activity history. Feature guide Use the search box to find a capability or workspace. Each row lists an area, feature, Try it here entry point and scope. Read the scope before assuming that visible metadata implies a corresponding processing feature. Rows marked as planned/unimplemented cannot be enabled by changing a setting. The guide is useful when deciding whether to inspect a native file, re-encode it or convert it. For example, CFA metadata can be preserved without debayering, and an ICC profile can be retained without a complete ICC color-management engine. Image generator Select Image generator. Choose a Sample format and Pixel layout. Set Width, Height and Channels. Optionally select Big-endian sample bytes. Click Create reference image. Select the new document and inspect, validate or export it. The generator accepts 1–2,048 pixels per axis and 1–4 channels. Supported sample formats are UInt8, UInt16, UInt32, UInt64, Float32, Float64, Complex32 and Complex64. Planar and interleaved layouts demonstrate the different linear storage orderings used by the sample inspector. Real-valued patterns use a horizontal gradient with channel offsets. Complex patterns include real and imaginary components. UInt64 repeats these exact values: 0, 1, 9007199254740993, 18446744073709551615. That makes it useful for observing why an exact integer inspector differs from Float64 statistics. To try this, generate a small UInt64 image, open Analyze, read four stored samples starting at zero, then compare a Float64 region view. The large integer representations need not match exactly after conversion to double. Generated files are demonstrations created by AstroView. They are not independent evidence of compatibility with another XISF/FITS producer. Complex and scientific cube samples remain inspectable even when a display preview is unavailable. Colour calculator Open Colour calculator, enter normalized Red/Green/Blue values and a Midtones parameter, then click Evaluate transforms. Results show XYZ, Lab, a Lab-to-RGB round trip, luminance and the midtones transfer of the red component. The calculator uses Core's default D50-adapted sRGB working space. It operates on the entered numbers and does not recolor the selected document. To change an image's preview, use Image → DISPLAY instead. The calculator is not an ICC profile editor or a photometric calibration tool. Reader policy Settings here apply to files opened after the changes. They do not replace the policy already captured by a previously opened lazy document. Close and reopen a file when you need it read under different settings. Setting Initial value Effect Maximum XISF block (MiB) 1024 Bounds an individual decoded XISF block Total decoded FITS bytes (MiB) 2047 Bounds retained raw FITS HDU payloads Strict FITS validation on open Off Rejects supported error-level conformance findings instead of retaining them in tolerant mode Allow network resources Off Permits a file to request supported network resources under the reader's policy Allow general external filesystem paths Off Permits supported general external block paths Allow header-relative paths outside the header directory Off Permits relative traversal outside the header's directory Network timeout (seconds) 30 Bounds supported network resource operations Header-directory-relative blocks remain enabled for distributed files. Keep the referenced block file beside its header when that is the intended layout; there is no need to allow arbitrary external paths just for a normal sibling XISB file. Core's other budgets remain at their defaults. Raising one setting does not remove every other limit, make decoding incremental, or ensure enough memory. Permit external access only when it is actually required by a file/location you intend to read. The app stays local for ordinary files under its default policy. Activity Activity records recent operations and results for the current workspace. Use it to confirm which files opened, which output path was saved and which operation failed or was canceled. It complements the status bar and error banner. It is not a persistent project/session file or an automatic backup of your edits.

desktop/index.html.title: AstroView user manual | AstroView documentation
desktop/index.html.summary: AstroView user manual AstroView is a desktop workspace for viewing and examining astronomical FITS and XISF images. You can inspect original samples and metadata, browse catalogs, calculate supported sky coordinates, check file integrity, and export copies with explicit control over conversion and storage. You do not need to write code to use the application. The separate Core developer guide covers programming against its library. This manual explains the controls you see in the desktop window. Start here Install and launch AstroView. Work through the reference-scene walkthrough. Open your own FITS, XISF or distributed XISH document. Inspect and validate it, then export a copy when ready. Find a task I want to… Go to Open several images and select a FITS extension Workspace and documents Brighten a dark preview, zoom or export a PNG Viewing images Find exposure/object metadata or add a note Metadata Measure sample statistics or inspect exact UInt64 values Analysis Browse a star catalog or create a typed XISF table Tables Translate a pixel position into RA/Dec Coordinates Check checksums, validate against a schema or sign a copy Integrity Change compression or convert FITS ↔ XISF Export Generate test data or allow a required external block Feature lab Understand an error or an unavailable preview Troubleshooting Three distinctions to keep in mind A display stretch changes the preview. It does not rewrite scientific pixel values. A PNG is a rendered display image; use a FITS/XISF export to retain scientific data and format metadata. Edits are held in memory. Apply a metadata/table/XML edit, then export a copy to save it. Close or exit after exporting anything you want to keep. The current workspace is not an automatically saved project or editing session. Conversion can omit information. The Export workspace reports supported transformations and omissions. Review it before allowing reported losses. About the illustrations The screenshots use AstroView's own synthetic reference scene, not a telescope photograph. They show AstroView 0.2.0 at a 1480 × 940 window size. Controls below the visible area are reached by scrolling. Number controls can reflect your operating system's decimal separator; free-text metadata and JSON follow the formats described in their chapters. Implemented features and remaining limitations are summarized in shortcuts, glossary and limits. For a detailed format support contract, consult the support matrix.

desktop/installation.html.title: Installation and launch | AstroView documentation
desktop/installation.html.summary: Installation and launch Choose the desktop download Open the repository's GitHub Releases and download AstroView.Desktop-<version>.zip. The separate Core archive is for developers and does not contain the graphical application. Extract the archive before launching. Choose your platform's directory: Directory Computer Start win-x64 64-bit Windows on x64 Double-click AstroView.exe linux-x64 Linux x64 with a glibc desktop environment Run ./AstroView in a terminal osx-arm64 macOS on Apple silicon Run ./AstroView in a terminal Each release executable includes the .NET runtime and native rendering libraries. An installed .NET SDK/runtime is not needed for these executables. Keep the license/notices files with any redistributed copy. The executable can run by itself after extraction; there is no installer or automatic file association. These release targets do not include Windows ARM, Linux ARM/musl or Intel macOS. The current macOS output is a command-line-launchable executable rather than a notarized .app bundle. Desktop executables are unsigned; follow your operating system's normal trusted-software approval process if it blocks launch. Linux and macOS permissions If your ZIP extractor did not retain executable permissions: chmod +x AstroView ./AstroView On Linux, use a supported graphical desktop with X11/XWayland, fontconfig and the .NET native prerequisites such as OpenSSL, ICU and zlib. A self-contained download still relies on these operating-system facilities. Launching in a display-less SSH session will not open the graphical workspace. On first launch, .NET extracts bundled native libraries into its temporary cache. The cache must be writable. An administrator can choose another location using DOTNET_BUNDLE_EXTRACT_BASE_DIR if the normal location is unavailable. Open files from a terminal Paths supplied as command-line arguments are opened in the workspace. Quote a path containing spaces: ./AstroView "/path/to/nebula.xisf" "/path/to/another exposure.fits" On Windows, launch AstroView.exe with the equivalent quoted paths. You can also open files after launch with Open images…, or drag supported files onto the window. Development builds and CI downloads If no release has been published, build from source with the .NET 10 SDK: dotnet restore AstroView.sln --locked-mode dotnet run --project src/AstroView.Desktop -c Release To supply files through dotnet run, put them after --. Ordinary CI desktop publish-directory artifacts require .NET 10; run dotnet AstroView.dll inside that downloaded directory. The Release workflow's desktop ZIP is the self-contained download described above. Installation check The executable accepts --self-test to check codecs, signatures and native rendering without opening a window. Exit code zero means the installation checks passed. It does not inspect your own photographs. On Linux/macOS: ./AstroView --self-test echo $? If launch or the installation check fails, see troubleshooting. Once the window opens, follow first steps.

desktop/integrity.html.title: Validation and signatures | AstroView documentation
desktop/integrity.html.summary: Validation and signatures Use Integrity to inspect semantic diagnostics, decode image payloads and check supported checksums/signatures. These checks answer different questions; read the result for the check you actually ran. Validate a document Select the document. Open Integrity and click Validate document. Wait for the operation to complete. Read the summary and the Severity, Code, Location and Finding columns. For XISF, this checks supported semantic structure and attempts to decode every primary image and available thumbnail. Declared block digests are checked when their data is accessed. For FITS, results include supported semantic diagnostics and checksum-card results. Result Meaning Error A supported validation/decoding check failed; inspect the affected location before using/exporting the result Warning Something needs attention but is not necessarily a complete read failure Info Context such as successful pixel decoding; read whether a digest actually existed No checksum present There was no corresponding digest to verify; this is different from a valid digest Opening a file and seeing a preview does not verify every image or ancillary block in a multi-image document. Likewise, a successful structure check is not a claim that every possible FITS/XISF convention is implemented. If a checksum fails, preserve the original file and check the source/copy rather than hiding the finding by removing its digest. A missing distributed block can allow header inspection while preventing a full integrity check. Validate against an XSD For XISF, Validate with XSD… lets you select a local schema file. Obtain the appropriate trusted schema for your required XISF revision/workflow. Click Validate with XSD… and select it. Read the resulting schema and semantic findings. The app does not silently fetch a universal schema from the internet. DTD and external network resolution are disabled for schema loading. A schema requiring external includes must be prepared for this local-resolution policy. XSD validation checks XML rules; it does not by itself prove that image blocks decode or that a document was signed by someone you trust. Verify a signature With a XISF document selected, click Verify signature. Read the signature summary rather than assuming that every file is signed. Verification checks signed XML using the embedded key. It does not authenticate a person's identity or establish that the embedded key belongs to a trusted producer. Run document validation/payload decoding as well if you need the declared data digests checked. XML signature verification and decoding every image are separate actions. Sign a demonstration copy Sign a copy (session key)… demonstrates creating a signed XISF copy. Select a XISF document and review any edits. Click Sign a copy (session key)…. Choose a new output name. Reopen the result and click Verify signature. Run Validate document to inspect its payloads too. The operation generates a temporary RSA key and discards the private key after the operation. It is not an identity certificate manager or a way to reuse a saved signing identity later. The public verification material travels with the signed document. Editing or re-encoding signed content can invalidate or remove its earlier signature. Sign the resulting copy again after the intended changes. Existing unprotected data blocks may also need checksum-bearing re-encoding before a document can be signed under the required block-integrity rules.

desktop/metadata.html.title: Inspecting and editing metadata | AstroView documentation
desktop/metadata.html.summary: Inspecting and editing metadata Use Inspect to find file properties, FITS cards and ancillary metadata. The workspace has Fields, Source header and XISF XML editor subtabs. Find a value Select the document and image/HDU in the sidebar. Open Inspect → Fields. Enter a keyword, property ID, value or scope in the search box. Read Field, Type, Value and Scope together. For example, search for Exposure, OBJECT, Telescope or checksum depending on the source format. A similarly named document property and image property can refer to different objects. Selecting another image can change the visible fields. Some values are formatted summaries of arrays or binary objects. To inspect the structural representation, open Source header. For XISF it displays XML; for FITS it displays the selected header's cards. This view is read-only. Edit a scalar property Select a row to populate the editor, or enter a new property ID. Choose Image property, Document property, Creation property or FITS keyword, as appropriate. Choose the scalar type and enter the value. Optionally enter a comment. Click Apply metadata edit and check the resulting field and scope. Export a copy to save it. For an application note, use an identifier such as AstroView:Note and type String. Creation metadata is reserved for XISF: identifiers; use your own namespace for application-specific properties. Identifiers in XISF are case-sensitive, so AstroView:Note and AstroView:note are different properties. Type Example input Notes String Reviewed before stacking Enter plain text, without extra XML quoting Boolean true Use true/false Int64 -42 Signed 64-bit integer UInt64 18446744073709551615 Exact unsigned integer text Float64 180.5 Use a decimal point in this free-text editor TimePoint 2026-11-01T22:15:00+00:00 Include an explicit offset for an unambiguous instant The free-text metadata editor uses invariant numeric formatting even if numeric spin controls elsewhere display a decimal comma. Numeric text such as 180,5 can be misinterpreted; use 180.5. XISF vectors, matrices and other advanced types use the XML editor or the separate table editor. Edit FITS keywords For a FITS file, the editor writes a keyword in the selected HDU header (or the primary header when appropriate). For an XISF image, choose FITS keyword to edit its embedded FITS-keyword metadata. Enter String values as ordinary text; the application performs the required FITS quoting. Avoid editing structural cards such as BITPIX or NAXIS to try to change an image's dimensions. A header edit does not resize its pixel payload. Core guards inconsistent structure when writing. The scalar editor is also not a specialized editor for repeated HISTORY/COMMENT card sequences; inspect those in the source header and preserve them through a native copy. Advanced XISF XML editing Open XISF XML editor. Click Load current XML to start from the currently selected document. Make a small, intentional change, retaining the XML namespace and structure. Click Apply XML in memory. Review fields and run Integrity → Validate document. Export a new copy and reopen it to check the result. Keep original block references valid. Deleting/changing an attachment location, sample format, geometry or compression attribute without changing the associated data can make the document unreadable. Arbitrary source pixels are not edited by typing a different number into a header attribute. Applying edited XML reparses supported structure; it does not write to the original file. Editing a signed document can invalidate its signature. After intentional content changes, export and sign the resulting copy again if a new signature is required. See integrity.

desktop/quick-start.html.title: First steps with the reference scene | AstroView documentation
desktop/quick-start.html.summary: First steps with the reference scene This walkthrough needs no files or internet connection. It introduces viewing, measurement, metadata and output before you work on your own observations. 1. Explore the four reference images On a normal empty launch, AstroView creates its reference scene. If you opened files at launch instead, click Reference scene to add a reference document. Select Reference scene.xisf in DOCUMENTS, then Emission nebula under IMAGES & HDUs. The scene includes: Item Purpose Emission nebula Float32 RGB preview, observation metadata, native astrometry and a star catalog UInt16 gradient Integer samples and histogram bounds Scientific cube Additional scientific axes without a general cube-plane preview Complex wave Complex-valued samples available in the sample inspector The nebula is generated demonstration data. It is not a real exposure or an independent test of another application's format implementation. 2. Change the view Select the Image workspace. Click Fit, then use the mouse wheel to zoom in. Drag the image to pan, and double-click to fit it again. Change the display mode from Auto stretch to Linear. Click Apply display, compare the preview, then restore Auto stretch. A darker linear preview is expected for many faint images. The scientific samples remain unchanged throughout this exercise. See viewing for linked channels, shadow clipping and PNG output. 3. Run an analysis Select Analyze with the emission nebula still selected. Choose channel 0, bounds 0 to 1, and 256 bins. Leave the statistics sample limit at 250000 and click Run analysis. Read the histogram totals and the three channel-statistics rows. The histogram counts every sample in its chosen channel. Statistics can be sampled, so the finite counts in the statistics table need not equal the histogram count. To try integer bounds, select UInt16 gradient, set histogram bounds to 0 and 65535, then run analysis again. 4. Add a note Return to Emission nebula and choose Inspect → Fields. In the metadata editor, select Image property. Enter key AstroView:Note, type String, and value First inspection. Click Apply metadata edit. Search for AstroView:Note in the fields list and confirm its value/scope. The note is in the open document's memory. It has not been written to disk. 5. Browse the catalog and coordinates Open Tables and select the reference-star catalog. Notice that large integer identifiers retain exact text. Then open Coordinates, enter image column 512 and row 384, and click Calculate sky coordinates. Click Calculate image coordinates to transform the resulting RA/Dec back. AstroView uses zero-based image positions and degrees for sky angles in this workspace. See coordinates before entering RA in another unit. 6. Validate and save a copy Open Integrity and click Validate document. Review the diagnostic list, including payload-decoding information. Open Export and select Keep native document. Click Export document… and save as reference-reviewed.xisf in a new location. Reopen that file and find your AstroView:Note in Inspect. This confirms that the in-memory note was saved. To share a picture rather than a scientific document, use Image → Export preview as PNG… instead. You can now open your own documents and follow the same inspect → validate → export workflow.

desktop/reference.html.title: Shortcuts, glossary and limits | AstroView documentation
desktop/reference.html.summary: Shortcuts, glossary and limits Keyboard and mouse reference Action Input Open documents Ctrl+O; Command+O on macOS Export document Ctrl+E Fit preview Ctrl+0 or Fit Actual-size preview Ctrl+1 or 1:1 Cancel a cancellable operation Escape or Cancel Zoom Mouse wheel Pan Left drag Fit again Double-click Select an image pixel Click The macOS Command shortcut is explicitly provided for opening files. The other listed keyboard gestures use Ctrl as shown; their corresponding buttons remain available on every platform. Common units and conventions Value Convention Image column/row in the UI Zero-based pixel centres RA and Dec in Coordinates Degrees, not RA hours Channel Zero-based index Stored-sample start Zero-based linear sample index Metadata/JSON numeric text Decimal point, invariant formatting TimePoint example ISO timestamp with an offset Reader budgets shown in MiB 1 MiB = 1,048,576 bytes Display shadow clipping Sigma parameter for the display stretch Numeric spin controls can follow the operating system's decimal separator. That does not change the invariant syntax required by metadata text and JSON. Interactive limits Tool Limit/default Window Minimum 1100 × 720; scroll internal panels for controls below the visible area Statistics Initial limit 250,000 samples/channel; controls allow up to 10,000,000 Histogram 256 bins initially; 8–4,096 bins Stored-sample text 1–256 samples per read Region text At most 4,096 total samples including all channels Table browser 200 rows and 16 data columns per page JSON table editor 1–32 fields, up to 1,000 rows, 4,096 elements/array cell; embedded-block size also applies Image generator 1–2,048 pixels/axis and 1–4 channels These are interactive application limits, not an exhaustive statement of Core's format limits. File readers also enforce independent byte, XML, dimension, decompression and table budgets. Glossary Term Meaning in AstroView FITS Astronomical file format organized into ordered header/data units HDU Header/data unit; can hold an image, table or another extension XISF Extensible image serialization format with image and metadata objects XISH / XISB Distributed XML header / referenced binary block file Scientific sample Numeric source value used for measurement and scientific output Preview 8-bit-per-component display rendering of the scientific samples Stretch Display transformation that makes a range of sample values visible Planar / interleaved Channels stored in separate planes / alternating within pixels Byte order Little-endian or big-endian byte representation of numeric components Checksum/digest Stored value used to detect a mismatch in covered content XML signature Signed XML integrity information, distinct from identity trust WCS / astrometry Metadata/model relating image positions to sky positions MAD Median absolute deviation, a measure of sampled dispersion CFA Color-filter-array mosaic description; not a debayering operation Native preservation Writing the native document model while retaining supported content Re-encoding Serializing editable content with new storage settings Conversion finding A report of preserved, transformed or omitted content Current capability boundaries AstroView exposes the capabilities implemented by Core. Current limitations include general complex magnitude/phase previews, scientific cube-plane viewing, native FITS table editing, compressed/tiled FITS image decoding, broader FITS WCS/distortion evaluation, debayering, full ICC processing and general streaming or memory-mapped image processing. The seven projections in the synthetic/native-XISF calculator do not imply seven implemented FITS WCS projection families. Inspectable CFA/ICC metadata does not imply that those processing operations are available. A feature listed as planned in Feature lab cannot be enabled through a different export setting. Use the support matrix for read/write/edit/preserve/evaluate details and the roadmap for planned work. The Core developer guide explains API integration separately from this user manual.

desktop/tables.html.title: Tables and catalogs | AstroView documentation
desktop/tables.html.summary: Tables and catalogs The Tables workspace browses supported FITS ASCII/binary and XISF typed tables. XISF documents can also create or replace a document-level table through a JSON definition. Browse a table Select the document containing your table. Open Tables → Table browser. Choose a table from the dropdown. Read its column headings and types, then navigate the rows/columns. The browser displays up to 200 rows and 16 data columns per page. Use Previous 200 / Next 200 for row pages and ← Columns / Columns → for column pages. The summary shows the displayed ranges and total size. An unresponsive navigation button at the first/last page simply means there is no further page in that direction. Integer scalar cells retain exact text, including Int64/UInt64 identifiers too large to represent exactly as doubles. Array cells are summarized rather than expanded into thousands of grid cells. A formatted summary is not a replacement for the underlying typed table data. If there are no tables, check the selected document and its image/HDU entries. An image-only file legitimately has no catalog. The reference scene includes a 48-row star table you can use to learn the browser. Create a XISF table Open a XISF document or create the reference scene. Select XISF table editor. Click Load example definition. Modify its identifier, fields or rows, retaining valid JSON. Click Apply table in memory. Return to Table browser, select the new table and check its values. Export the document to save the change. A definition follows this structure: { "id": "UserCatalog", "caption": "My reference stars", "fields": [ { "id": "Name", "type": "String" }, { "id": "Flux", "type": "Float64" }, { "id": "Flags", "type": "I32Vector" } ], "rows": [ ["Star A", 1234.5, [1, 0, 1]], ["Star B", 890.25, [0, 1, 0]] ] } id identifies the document-level table. Applying the same identifier replaces that table; a different identifier adds another table. caption is a human-readable description. Each field has an identifier and type; an optional header supplies its heading. Every row must have one cell per field in the same order. JSON requires quoted strings, unquoted numeric values, true/false for Boolean values and decimal points in numbers. A TimePoint uses an ISO-style timestamp string such as "2026-11-01T22:15:00+00:00". Types and limits The interactive editor supports scalar String, Boolean, TimePoint, signed/unsigned integer and real types, plus integer/real vectors and rectangular matrices. Use types such as Int64, UInt64, Float32, Float64, I32Vector and F64Matrix. A vector cell is a JSON array; a matrix cell is an array of rows with equal lengths. The editor accepts 1–32 fields, up to 1,000 rows and up to 4,096 elements in an array cell. Embedded cell-block storage can impose an additional size limit; use a smaller cell if the editor reports that it exceeds its block limit. These limits apply to the interactive editor, not to every table the reader can browse. FITS editing and conversion FITS tables are readable but are not editable through this JSON editor. Preserve the native document when retaining their original storage is important. Converting FITS tables to XISF can transform or omit table-storage details, units, scaling and array representations. Review Analyze fidelity rather than assuming that a displayed table can be recreated unchanged in either format. Advanced XISF types outside the JSON editor remain accessible through the full XISF XML editor or the developer API. Use the XML editor only when you understand the format's block/type requirements.

desktop/troubleshooting.html.title: Troubleshooting | AstroView documentation
desktop/troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting Start with the error banner and Feature lab → Activity. Check the selected document/image, the operation you ran and the path it reports before changing settings or trying another export. Launch problems Symptom Check and next step Executable does not start Extract the ZIP first and choose the correct OS/architecture directory Permission denied on Linux/macOS Restore executable permission with chmod +x AstroView macOS blocks the download The executable is unsigned/not notarized; use your system's normal trusted-software approval process Missing .NET runtime A framework-dependent CI publish folder needs .NET 10; use the self-contained Release desktop ZIP if available Native library/display error Check the platform's graphical/native prerequisites and a writable .NET bundle cache No window over SSH/headless session Use a graphical desktop to launch the UI; --self-test checks installation without a display The self-test checks the installation, not the validity of a particular image. See installation for the download types and command-line launch. A file does not open Confirm that it is a supported FITS/XISF/XISH document rather than another type with a renamed extension. Check filesystem permissions and whether another program is still writing it. For distributed XISF, locate the referenced XISB file and keep its relative path valid. If an error mentions a budget, review Feature lab → Reader policy and the file's expected size. A compressed file can expand far beyond its download size. Raising a budget does not bypass a missing codec or every implementation array/memory limit. Reopen the file after changing the reader policy. Strict FITS validation can reject a file that tolerant mode opens with findings. If your workflow permits tolerant inspection, disable strict-on-open for a new read and examine the findings. Do not equate tolerant opening with full format conformance. The viewport is blank or dark Situation What to do Faint real image in Linear mode Select Auto stretch and click Apply display Empty FITS primary HDU Select a later image extension in IMAGES & HDUs Table/unknown extension selected Use Inspect or Tables rather than expecting image pixels Complex image or general scientific cube Use the stored-sample inspector; a general preview is not implemented Three-plane FITS known to be RGB Enable Interpret 3rd axis as RGB/RGBA and apply it Missing/bad data block Run Integrity validation and inspect the decoding error Do not label a three-axis scientific cube RGB simply to force a picture. That can change the interpretation used by a subsequent conversion. Measurements look wrong Check histogram bounds against the scientific sample range. A UInt16 image often needs a much larger range than 0 to 1. Check the chosen channel and include underflow/overflow/non-finite counts when comparing totals. Statistics use a sample limit, while the histogram counts the complete chosen channel. Normalized statistics and manually chosen histogram bounds are separate. Display stretch is another separate transformation. For very large integers, compare Exact stored samples rather than expecting all Float64 region or statistics values to retain exact text. If a region read fails, check its X/Y, width/height, channel and 4,096-sample interactive limit. That limit counts all channels, even though only the selected channel is printed. Edits are missing Did you click Apply metadata edit, Apply table in memory or Apply XML in memory before exporting? Did you save the whole document or an isolated image? Document-level content remains in the original when an image is isolated. Reopen the actual exported path and inspect the correct scope/image. Closing a document or exiting before export loses in-memory edits. The workspace does not automatically persist an editing session. A preview PNG cannot retain the scientific document's properties or tables. For free-text numeric metadata, use decimal points and an explicit TimePoint offset. For JSON, check quotes, commas, row lengths and field types. Applying an existing document-level table identifier replaces that table rather than adding a differently named one. Export is rejected Choose a new output name when a path is an active source. For distributed output, choose a new header filename and retain its generated sibling block file. If conversion findings report omitted content, review the report. Select Allow reported conversion losses only if that output is acceptable. The setting does not enable unsupported pixel types. To preserve a native document instead, choose Keep native document. If a requested SHA-3 digest is unavailable on your platform, choose a supported digest such as SHA-256. If a signature fails after metadata edits or re-encoding, export the intended final content and sign that copy again. The operation is slow or uses substantial memory Analysis/regions can decode a complete block, and typed values plus a preview can coexist in memory. Close unneeded documents, use smaller generated examples for experiments and avoid opening many very large files together. A statistics sample limit does not make the full block decode streaming. Use Cancel/Escape when offered, allowing for codecs that finish their current block. During output publication, cancellation can be disabled. Do not repeatedly start new operations while the status bar shows the previous one is still busy. Report a reproducible issue Record the AstroView version, OS/architecture, file format, operation, selected sample type/dimensions, relevant reader/export settings and exact error/finding code. Prefer a small shareable example or a reference-scene/generator recipe. Remove private observation metadata, paths and credential-bearing resource URLs before sharing logs or files. A screenshot of the error plus the steps that led to it is more useful than an unexplained blank viewport.

desktop/viewing.html.title: Viewing images | AstroView documentation
desktop/viewing.html.summary: Viewing images The Image workspace presents a display rendering of the selected scientific image. The dimensions/sample summary above it describes the underlying data, not an 8-bit conversion of that data. Navigate the image Control Result Fit / Ctrl+0 Fits the preview in the available viewport 1:1 / Ctrl+1 Sets actual-size viewing Mouse wheel Zooms the view Left drag Pans the image Double-click Fits the image again Click Selects a pixel and updates the position readout Selection crosshair Shows/hides the selection marker Pixel positions shown by the workspace are zero-based image positions. Source orientation is accounted for when mapping a displayed selection. Panning and zooming do not crop, resize or rotate the stored scientific image. Choose a display mode In the right-hand DISPLAY panel, choose a mode and click Apply display. Scroll the panel if lower controls are outside the window. Mode Use it when Auto stretch You want faint astronomical structure to be visible without manually scaling source samples Linear You want a preview based on linear normalization, for example to inspect an integer gradient Stored display function The file contains display settings you want AstroView to use Target background controls the automatic stretch's background target. The application starts at 0.22. Shadows clipping (σ) adjusts the shadow clipping parameter; the initial value is -2.8. These are display controls, not changes to black-level calibration in the original data. With Link colour channels selected, the stretch links channels rather than independently stretching each channel. Try linked channels first for an RGB image; independent channel stretches can change apparent color balance. Compare the result visually and use Analyze for the actual sample measurements. A file may lack a meaningful stored display function. Do not interpret that as missing pixel data; try Auto stretch or Linear. Different display modes can make the same scientific samples appear quite different. Observation summary The OBSERVATION panel summarizes recognized object, telescope, exposure and filter metadata. Missing fields are left out; the app does not infer a missing exposure or telescope from the image appearance. Use Inspect for individual metadata values and scope. FITS color-axis interpretation A third FITS axis is preserved as a scientific axis by default. If your file is known to store RGB/RGBA planes in that axis: Select the FITS image. Scroll to FITS AXES. Select Interpret 3rd axis as RGB/RGBA. Click Apply axis interpretation. Use this only when the third axis really represents color. A cube with three spectral planes is not automatically an RGB photograph. This choice also informs subsequent format conversion; review it before exporting. Export the visible rendering Click Export preview as PNG… and choose a new filename. The PNG represents the rendered preview, including the chosen display transformation and supported orientation/color interpretation. It does not retain scientific sample precision, the whole FITS/XISF document or its catalog metadata. Use Export for a scientific document copy. When there is no preview Complex-valued images and general scientific cubes remain available to inspection, but do not have a general magnitude/phase or cube-plane bitmap renderer in the current implementation. Use Analyze → Exact stored samples and Inspect. A table HDU or empty primary HDU can also legitimately have no preview. See troubleshooting before changing reader limits.

desktop/workspace.html.title: Workspace and documents | AstroView documentation
desktop/workspace.html.summary: Workspace and documents Window layout The top bar contains Reference scene and Open images…. The left sidebar has two lists: DOCUMENTS selects a file/session; IMAGES & HDUs selects an item inside that document. The title and summary above the workspaces describe the current selection. The eight workspaces are Image, Inspect, Analyze, Tables, Coordinates, Integrity, Export and Feature lab. Switching workspace does not save or convert the selected document. Some workspaces expose the whole document, while others operate on the selected image. The status bar shows the current operation and cancellation availability. Errors appear in a banner near the top; Dismiss hides the message after you have read it. Dismissing an error does not complete the failed operation. Open files Use Open images… or Ctrl+O (Command+O on macOS). You can select several files in one picker operation. FITS extensions commonly use .fits, .fit or .fts; XISF uses .xisf; distributed headers use .xish. Drag supported files onto the window or pass paths on the command line as an alternative. AstroView examines file content when detecting its format. Renaming an unrelated file to .xisf does not make it readable. Raster pictures such as JPEG and PNG are not the astronomical document formats opened by this workspace. When a batch contains an unreadable file, read the error banner/activity history and check which documents actually opened. Do not assume every selected file succeeded merely because one image appears. Select an image or extension Choose the document in DOCUMENTS. Select the desired entry in IMAGES & HDUs. Check the dimensions, sample type and channel count above the tabs. Choose a workspace suitable for that entry. A FITS primary HDU can be empty; a later extension may hold the image. A table or unknown extension can have useful metadata without an image preview. Use Inspect and Tables rather than treating every blank viewport as a failed file load. An XISF document can contain several images. Selecting one does not remove the others. Export document… exports the document; use Isolate selected image as a new document first when you want only one image. Keep distributed files together A .xish file is a header that can reference a sibling .xisb block file. Open the header, keep the referenced file beside it, and retain both files while working. A document can open its header successfully and fail later when pixels or an ancillary block are accessed if a block file is missing. Default policy permits header-relative sibling blocks. Network access, general external filesystem paths and traversal outside the header directory are off. Change a policy only if required for a file you intend to access; the reader settings chapter explains how changes apply. Changes, closing and cancellation Metadata, XML and table edits are applied in memory. Export a copy before closing a document or exiting if you want to keep those edits. The application does not provide a persistent project/session or automatic saving of the workspace. Select a document and click Close to remove it and release retained previews and data. Large documents can use considerable memory, particularly after analysis or preview rendering. Closing documents you no longer need is useful even when their source files are compressed. Long operations temporarily disable conflicting controls. Use Cancel or Escape when cancellation is offered. Some codecs finish their current block before returning. Output publication can temporarily disable cancellation while committing a file. After a canceled open, the app restores the earlier selection where possible; inspect the document list before continuing.

image-formats.html.title: FITS and XISF support | AstroView documentation
image-formats.html.summary: FITS and XISF support For complete integration guidance and executable examples, use the Core developer guide and API reference guide. All APIs live in AstroView.Core. The portable XISFLib.Net core was imported from commit 9c0325fcda231603014c497d4d5bbd40477e9030; it is now compiled into AstroView.Core with no XISFLib dependency. Source folders retain their upstream organization (Fits, Xisf, Imaging, Astronomy, Internal). Original type names are retained, including the Xisf prefix. Reading and writing using AstroView.Core; // Typed image creation copies the supplied samples. var image = XisfImageData.FromSamples(new ushort[] { 0, 100, 200, 65535 }, [2, 2], 1); image.Properties.Set(XisfKnownProperties.Observation.Object.Name, "M31"); XisfWriter.Write("image.xisf", [image], new XisfWriterOptions { Compression = XisfCompression.Zstd, Checksum = XisfChecksum.Sha256 }); var loaded = XisfReader.Load("image.xisf"); ushort[] scientificPixels = loaded.Images[0].GetSamples<ushort>(); var preview = XisfDisplayRenderer.Render(loaded.Images[0], XisfStretchOptions.Auto); // preview.Pixels contains BGRA32 display pixels; scientific samples are unchanged. var hdu = FitsHdu.CreateImage(FitsImage.FromPhysicalSamples( new ushort[] { 0, 100, 200, 65535 }, [2, 2]), true); FitsWriter.Write("image.fits", new FitsDocument([hdu]), new FitsWriterOptions { WriteChecksums = true }); var fits = FitsReader.Load("image.fits"); double[] physicalPixels = fits.Images.First().GetPhysicalSamples(); Dimensions are width, height, then further axes. FromArray uses [height, width] or [height, width, channel]. Parsed typed reads default to planar channel order. FITS scientific axes remain scientific axes unless RGB/RGBA interpretation is explicitly selected. Physical-double reads cannot retain every Int64/UInt64 integer exactly above 2^53; use the exact typed conversion paths when that precision is required. FitsConverter converts between the two image models. Cross-format conversion can omit metadata or unsupported content: the default loss policy rejects such conversions. Explicitly opt into ConversionLossPolicy.Allow only after reviewing the conversion findings. Ownership and validation Caller streams remain open. XISF stream loads buffer their input; path loads lazily reopen the source for data blocks. Keep source files available and unchanged while using lazy data, including metadata blocks. ToEditable() supports edits to parsed content; inspecting a document's XML returns a detached copy. XISF checksums are checked when blocks are decoded, so loading the header alone does not verify every pixel block. FITS exposes validation diagnostics and optional checksum results. Missing FITS checksums have nullable results. Reader options bound resources and decompression; default XISF options disable network and general external-path access. Embedded signature integrity does not establish signer trust. Single-file path writers stage output before replacement; distributed XISF output and caller-provided streams do not provide the same transactional guarantee. Dependencies and verification LZ4 (K4os.Compression.LZ4), Zstandard (ZstdSharp.Port), and Microsoft XML cryptography are runtime NuGet dependencies. No Windows/UI or viewer package is required. Attribution and codec licenses are included in package output. The imported regression suite covers generated format fixtures, compression, checksums, signatures, metadata, numeric boundaries, malformed input, conversions, and rendering baselines. Additional on-disk tests use hand-constructed FITS/XISF bytes. Upstream external photograph corpus tests and batch-converter application tests are excluded, including the converter-specific assertions in metadata tests. These tests do not establish interoperability with every real-world file variant.

interoperability.html.title: Independent interoperability evidence | AstroView documentation
interoperability.html.summary: Independent interoperability evidence Phase 1 adds 60 small independently serialized fixtures and reverse-direction checks using development-only reference tools. The library has no Python, Astropy, or Python XISF runtime dependency. Committed corpus tests/AstroView.Core.Tests/Fixtures/Interoperability/manifest.json records producer versions, each file's SHA-256, expected geometry, exact sample values, metadata and independent Astropy WCS reference points. Fixture pixel values and metadata in the original 14 fixtures are original synthetic data. The additional 46 external fixtures retain their source revisions, hashes and MIT notices in the libxisf/ and external/ subdirectories. No telescope photographs are redistributed as part of the local corpus; the committed external samples have their own MIT repository provenance. Producer Evidence Astropy 8.0.2 UInt16 offsets, exact UInt64 boundaries, Float32 cube, multiple HDUs, binary table Int64/Float32/logical/vector columns, checksums and plain TAN coordinates Python xisf 0.9.7 UInt8/16/32 and Float32/64, planar mono/RGB, uncompressed/zlib/LZ4/LZ4HC/Zstandard with shuffle, UTF-8/string/vector properties and quoted FITS metadata libXISF via xisf-rs corpus generator 40 independent codec/type files, monochrome and RGB, exact producer-defined byte patterns and typed channel access including IEEE floating-point bits PixInsight files from MIT repositories Six compatibility/negative cases: attached/embedded storage, embedded zlib, two-channel pixels, shuffled zlib/SHA-256, and missing thumbnail attachments InteroperabilityTests verifies all file hashes and independently specified pixels/metadata without Python or network access. The independent FITS table exposed and now protects the omitted-repeat-count default in TFORM. Reverse checksum verification also motivated conventional standard-card comment alignment. LibXisfInteroperabilityTests checks all 40 libXISF files against the upstream generator's deterministic byte pattern, not values derived with AstroView. LocalXisfExampleTests.SmallExternalSamplesMatchIndependentPixelsAndKnownStorageDefects runs six small external cases offline on all three CI platforms. Their independent pixel expectations come from Python xisf for attached images and a separate Python standard-library base64/zlib oracle for embedded images. The manifest records which oracle was used. The two truncated thumbnail cases deliberately require complete saves to fail while leaving their primary images accessible. Reverse-direction checks tools/AstroView.Interop writes one checksummed FITS image and five XISF images, one per codec including uncompressed. Astropy and Python xisf read these exports and compare known pixels and metadata. Astropy additionally verifies FITS checksums. CI performs these checks separately from the three-platform offline .NET suite. It also checks all 40 original libXISF files and AstroView's preserving rewrites against the independent producer pattern using Python xisf. python -m pip install setuptools==84.2.1 wheel==0.48.0 python -m pip install --no-build-isolation -r tools/interop/requirements.txt dotnet run --project tools/AstroView.Interop -c Release -- artifacts/interop/exports python tools/interop/fixtures.py verify python tools/interop/xisf_samples.py verify-fixtures python tools/interop/xisf_samples.py verify-fixtures --directory artifacts/interop/exports/libxisf Use an isolated virtual environment for the Python tools. To intentionally regenerate the committed corpus, run python tools/interop/fixtures.py generate and review both binaries and manifest changes. Producers write creation times and checksum comments, so regeneration can change byte hashes without changing pixels. Expected values come from generator input, not from decoding with AstroView. The pinned tools retain their own licenses: Astropy is BSD-3-Clause, Python xisf is GPL-3.0, NumPy is BSD-3-Clause, and their codec dependencies retain their own notices. No source from those tools is copied into AstroView or its NuGet package. Running a separate development tool does not make it a library dependency. The synthetic fixture data have their own redistribution notice alongside the manifest. Local photographs and real producer files Fixtures/LocalXisf/manifest.json records provenance, original file hashes and independent pixel hashes for 73 local XISF files containing 79 primary images (2,739,639,831 original file bytes). The images remain outside Git at C:\Code\AstroExamples\XISF. Python xisf decoded 75 images; four embedded images were checked separately with the standard-library oracle. All 79 match AstroView's decoded bytes. The existing 11 local FITS files remain separate. The opt-in local XISF test verifies every original hash, geometry, sample type, layout and independently decoded pixel hash. It then saves/reloads the 71 complete files, compares the independent pixel expectations again and checks preservation of the original XML metadata, allowing changed attachment offsets and added block digests. Twelve files contain legacy PCL:AstrometricSolution:* metadata, which survives that save path. These tests prove preservation, not coordinate evaluation. All attached serialized blocks are also hashed directly from the original and rewritten files, including thumbnails and binary property matrices/vectors. The two incomplete samples must reject thumbnail access and complete saving. Semantic validation diagnostics remain in the optional local report. Existing files trigger findings for missing explicit UTF-8 declarations, legacy creation time typing and ICC flags. Pixel compatibility does not mean strict conformance. See testing for commands and report paths. Regenerate independent expectations explicitly, then review the manifest diff: python tools/interop/xisf_samples.py record-local --corpus C:/Code/AstroExamples/XISF python tools/interop/xisf_samples.py import-fixtures --corpus C:/Code/AstroExamples/XISF python tools/interop/xisf_samples.py import-embedded --corpus C:/Code/AstroExamples/XISF The local sample provenance is documentation of public availability and stated usage terms, not permission to redistribute the photographs. Only small fixtures distributed by MIT repositories are committed, with their notices. Coverage gaps — AV-002 remains partial The new corpus is independent evidence for the combinations above, not a claim of universal producer compatibility or complete XISF conformance. In particular: No independently produced real native XISF astrometric/distortion solution with confirmed redistribution permission is available in the current corpus. Independently produced distributed XISF, XISF tables, complex/UInt64 pixels, big-endian and interleaved files are not yet represented. Python xisf's writer does not cover all of these capabilities. Existing generated .NET tests remain useful regressions but do not close the independent-producer evidence gap. Python xisf 0.9.7 fails on embedded image data (KeyError: value); embedded images are therefore excluded from its reverse-reader checks. AstroView's embedded-image tests are separate; the reference tool is not patched to pass. Native astrometry must not be confused with the legacy PCL: properties in twelve local files. No local file has a native AstrometricSolution:* solution. AV-001 and AV-003 can be completed independently. AV-002 stays unchecked until the remaining independently produced fixtures, provenance/permissions, and reference expectations are collected. Add files and tests incrementally without relabeling AstroView-generated fixtures as independent producer data. Reference implementations: Astropy FITS, Astropy WCS, Python xisf.
