releases.html.title: GitHub releases | AstroView documentation
releases.html.summary: GitHub releases The Release Actions workflow creates a GitHub Release when a matching version tag is pushed. It adds two downloads: Asset Contents AstroView.Desktop-<version>.zip One self-contained executable per platform: Windows x64, Linux x64 (glibc), macOS Apple silicon. Includes .NET and native rendering libraries. AstroView.Core-<version>.zip Core DLL, required compression/cryptography DLLs, XML documentation, an MSBuild reference file and the normal Core NuGet package. No desktop assemblies. GitHub also supplies its standard source-code ZIP and tarball automatically. Both AstroView archives contain notices, usage instructions and a manifest with the version and each file's SHA-256. Release notes include both archive hashes. Single-file .NET applications are specific to an OS and CPU architecture; a single executable cannot serve all platforms. Each desktop executable can run by itself. Native libraries extract to .NET's temporary bundle cache at launch. Normal OS prerequisites still apply. The archive README explains execution permissions, supported targets and the unsigned macOS executable (no .app or notarization). Executables are not trimmed, preserving Avalonia and XML signature reflection. .NET does not provide single-file publishing for a reusable managed class library. The Core archive therefore includes its required managed dependencies separately. Import its AstroView.Core.props in a .NET 10 project to reference the DLLs, or use its .nupkg through a local NuGet source. The package restores its dependencies normally; the direct DLL option works without a package restore for Core. Follow the archive README when cross-publishing a consumer with an explicit runtime ID. Publish a release Update eng/Versions.props and CHANGELOG.md; commit and push the changes. Create a matching tag, for example git tag v0.2.0 or git tag v0.2.0-rc.1. Push that tag: git push origin v0.2.0 (use the actual tag). Watch Release in Actions. After all checks pass, the workflow creates the release, uploads both assets and publishes it. Prerelease tags automatically create GitHub prereleases. The workflow validates tags against the version policy. Publication uses the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN with contents: write only in the final job. No personal token or package-registry secret is needed. It requires the remote tag to exist and never overwrites an existing release. The GitHub CLI stages the release as a draft while uploading, so a failed upload cannot publish a partial release. If uploading fails, inspect/delete the incomplete draft before rerunning. Published versions should receive a new version/tag for corrections. This workflow does not publish to nuget.org. Creating a version commit or manually running the workflow does not create a GitHub Release. Validate without publishing Choose Actions → Release → Run workflow on the desired branch. This runs the same checks and produces a release-downloads workflow artifact containing the two ZIPs and release notes, but skips publication. Branch runs use the normal <version>-ci.<run>.<attempt> version. Every release run gates assembly/publication on: The existing Windows/Linux/macOS build, Core and headless desktop tests, version checks, NuGet packing and independent FITS/XISF reference-reader checks. Native self-contained publishing with locked runtime-specific dependencies. Running each executable with --self-test in a directory containing only that executable: all XISF codecs, FITS samples, XML/PKCS signatures, Core rendering and native Skia PNG encoding/decoding. This check does not require a display; workspace behavior is covered by the separate headless tests. Compiling/publishing/running an independent .NET consumer of each extracted Core archive, with no Core ProjectReference, no PackageReferences and cleared package sources; cross-publishing also verifies the target's cryptography DLL is selected. Archive contract tests, complete payloads, executable permissions, matching versions and SHA-256 manifests. Local packaging Use the .NET 10 SDK, Python 3.10+ and PowerShell on the target OS: ./eng/Build-Release.ps1 -Runtime win-x64 -Version 0.2.0-dev -Output artifacts/release-local Use linux-x64 or osx-arm64 on those platforms. Output must be a new directory. This script runs native installation checks and must run on the specified target platform. It builds the desktop payload and Core archive; CI combines the three desktop payloads into the final desktop ZIP using eng/release_archives.py. The ordinary project lock files remain platform-independent. Single-file release graphs have packages.release.<runtime>.lock.json in Core and Desktop. When changing packages or the SDK/runtime patch used for releases, intentionally regenerate each target graph and commit its updated locks: dotnet restore src/AstroView.Desktop -p:RuntimeIdentifier=win-x64 ` -p:PublishRuntimeIdentifier=win-x64 ` -p:AstroViewReleaseRuntime=win-x64 -p:PublishSingleFile=true ` -p:SelfContained=true -p:IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract=true ` -p:PublishTrimmed=false --force-evaluate Repeat for the other two RIDs. Do not disable locked restore in the release job. Set both runtime properties to the same RID: during restore, .NET 10 otherwise can also infer the host's publish runtime when single-file publishing is enabled.

reviews/2026-10-31-code-review.html.title: Code review — 2026-10-31 | AstroView documentation
reviews/2026-10-31-code-review.html.summary: Code review — 2026-10-31 Reviewed FITS parsing/writing/tables, XISF resources/codecs/references, image statistics/layouts/rendering, astronomy metadata/WCS, tests and packaging. Three parallel reviews were followed by independent cross-review of the patches. This is a source and regression review, not a formal security audit or proof of universal interoperability. Requested regression tests XisfMalformedInputRegressionTests protects both original malformed-input fixes: Non-seekable input with a complete preamble but truncated XML produces XisfFormatException with an inner EndOfStreamException. Sync and async entry points leave the caller stream open. Invalid Base64/hex characters and incomplete groups produce XisfFormatException with an inner FormatException at lazy access. Inline/embedded storage and repeat access after failure are covered. Ordinary storage IOException remains unchanged. Corrupt zlib now also retains its codec exception as the cause of a format error, for stream and path access. Findings fixed Priority describes the discovered consequence, not an outstanding blocker. Priority Defect and correction Regression tests P1 Recursive XISF references could exhaust the process stack. Iterative traversal preserves cycle detection and accepts 20,000-node shallow chains. XisfReferenceRegressionTests P1 Huge shuffle item sizes caused billions of empty iterations on tiny blocks. Return the owned tail immediately when there is no complete item. XisfResourceRegressionTests P1 XISF block limits were checked after allocating concatenated/decoded text or reading an external file. Preflight text nodes and opened-file length; also reject rooted cross-volume header-relative escapes. XisfResourceRegressionTests P1 Repeated FITS descriptors could amplify a small heap into huge decoded arrays. Debit a cumulative per-table element budget before allocating. FitsTableRegressionTests P1 Unsupported WCS projections/axes/distortions silently returned incorrect celestial coordinates. Reject unsupported explicit transforms; respect sparse CD defaults and CD precedence. WorldCoordinateRegressionTests P2 Empty FITS numeric/P/Q arrays divided by zero or read missing descriptors. Return typed empty values and reject invalid repeated descriptors. FitsTableRegressionTests P2 ASCII integers lost precision above 2^53, E vectors lost their float array type, and ASCII null markers failed parsing. Preserve Int64 values and types; recognize null text before conversion. FitsTableRegressionTests P2 FITS long strings split escaped apostrophes and dropped continuation comments. Split logical characters and preserve final comments. Reject unrepresentable ASCII/card content instead of silently replacing/truncating it. FitsLongStringRegressionTests P2 Distributed XISF paths assumed case-insensitive directories and rewrote legal Unix backslash filenames. Centralize platform-aware checks and preserve filenames. XisfWriterPathRegressionTests P2 Finite extremes overflowed median, histogram placement, mean, normalization or variance. Retain ordinary arithmetic with scaled fallbacks; use wide statistics sampling arithmetic. ImageStatisticsRegressionTests, ParsedNormalizationRegressionTests P2 XISF-carried FITS strings leaked quotes and prevented timestamp extraction. Decode once while native FITS strings retain their literal values. AstronomyMetadataRegressionTests Performance Invalid image requests decoded entire lazy images before failing. Run shared cheap validators before source access. ImageStatisticsRegressionTests Performance Statistics sorted twice and allocated a second sampled buffer. Exact selection reuses owned samples for MAD; extrema are retained before reordering. Independent sorted-reference statistics tests Measured performance dotnet run --project tools/AstroView.Performance -c Release Windows x64, .NET 10.0.14; one million samples, seed 314159; three warm-ups and seven measured iterations. Both implementations must return identical median/MAD. Distribution Two sorts / two buffers Selection / reused buffer Allocated bytes per operation Random 111.81 ms 23.58 ms 16,000,184 → 8,000,024 Sorted 98.90 ms 45.38 ms 16,000,184 → 8,000,024 Constant 36.26 ms 6.79 ms 16,000,184 → 8,000,024 Times are medians and isolate the median/MAD stage, not complete statistics or file-loading throughput. Timings vary by machine/runtime and are not CI assertions. Defensive copies, checksums and exact integer conversion paths remain intact. Readability and compatibility CelestialWorldCoordinateSystem now has its own file. A small internal helper shares FITS string decoding. Validation and distributed-path checks are centralized. Comments explain numeric slow paths, buffer ownership and iterative reference traversal. The existing exact-selection fallback and SIMD helpers are retained. The benchmark links the production selection source without widening public APIs. New FitsReaderOptions.MaximumTableElements defaults to 10,000,000 per table. Strings count characters, bit fields count bits, repeated heap references count each decoded element again. Raise it explicitly for larger trusted tables. Unscaled ASCII I cells now return long; scaled cells retain physical double values. Callers assuming all ASCII numbers were double must handle both types. FITS metadata that cannot fit printable ASCII/80-character cards throws rather than losing content. Failed single-file path writes preserve existing output. The WCS convenience API supports degree-based RA/DEC TAN in that axis order, plus its original linear mode when both CTYPE keywords are absent. Unsupported explicit conventions, pole overrides and distortion parameters are rejected. This does not change the separate native XISF astrometric evaluator. Remaining findings and profiling targets P2 — optional network body timeout: XISF applies NetworkTimeout to request and stream acquisition, but synchronous body copying does not observe cancellation. A server stalling after headers may outlive that timeout. Network access is disabled by default. Follow-up: cancellation-aware HTTP body reads plus a local stalling-server test. Arbitrary custom streams may require their own cancellation cooperation. Unmeasured performance opportunity: FITS numeric table decoding boxes elements and creates intermediate lists/arrays, including scalar cells. Benchmark real scalar/vector tables with scaling/nulls before adding specialized typed decoders. Unmeasured performance opportunity: rectangular-array image factories flatten then copy, matrix-property decoding boxes elements, and matching-type channel/region reads still have per-sample paths. Profile allocation and row-copy costs before changing ownership/layout contracts. Unmeasured performance opportunity: Lab rendering looks up working-space matrices per pixel. Benchmark an immutable per-render transform and define how caller mutation of working-space collections is handled before changing it. The network timeout is a known limitation, not a tested guarantee. The review does not claim universal maximum performance or absence of further defects. Validation and primary references Validation includes the full Release suite, locked restore, package generation, and the local 11-file FITS corpus. Photographs/reports remain outside tracked source. CI builds/tests on Windows, Linux and macOS; platform-specific tests explicitly skip where their filesystem assumptions do not apply. FITS 4.0, FITS WCS, SIP convention. Follow-up 2026-11-01: the network body-read timeout finding is resolved by AV-003. See Phase 1 interoperability and timeout evidence and the regression tests. Custom resolver code/streams still need to cooperate with cancellation.

roadmap.html.title: FITS/XISF development checklist | AstroView documentation
roadmap.html.summary: FITS/XISF development checklist Recorded: 2026-10-31. Status: in progress; unchecked items are not implemented promises. Work through the steps in order unless a dependency or a newly discovered defect requires a change. Keep the stable task IDs when splitting work into issues or PRs. Check a task only after its completion criteria and relevant tests pass. Starting point Ordinary multi-HDU FITS images, ASCII/binary table reading, scaling, image nulls, checksums, long strings and HIERARCH are already supported. XISF already supports monolithic/distributed containers, zlib/LZ4/LZ4HC/Zstandard, shuffling/subblocks, checksums, unsigned/real/complex pixels, rich properties, tables, ancillary metadata, signatures, and native astrometric solutions. The restricted FITS WCS helper is separate from the native XISF evaluator, which already supports seven projections and distortion models. Unsupported coordinate evaluation does not necessarily prevent loading pixels or preserving headers. The local example corpus contains eleven FITS files and 73 XISF files (79 images). This list comes from code inspection and the code review. It is not an exhaustive standards-conformance certification. Phase 1 — Define and independently verify the support contract [x] AV-001 — Publish a feature-support matrix. Track read, write, edit, preserve, and evaluate separately for each format feature. Distinguish native format requirements, optional conventions, and image-processing features. Done when: the matrix describes the current APIs accurately, links to tests, and explicitly identifies unsupported behaviour without claiming full conformance. [ ] AV-002 — Expand independent interoperability fixtures. Add redistributable FITS reference fixtures and independently produced XISF examples covering codecs, sample types, layouts, containers, tables, and real astrometric solutions. Keep large/private photographs local and record provenance and hashes. Done when: tests compare independently known pixels/metadata, and files written here are checked with independent readers. Reference tools are development tools, not required runtime dependencies. [x] AV-003 — Close the optional external-resource timeout gap. Make HTTP body reads observe cancellation/timeouts; document cooperation required from custom resolver streams. Preserve default-disabled network access. Done when: a local test server stalling after headers is cancelled, caller ownership remains correct, and no real external service is needed by tests. Phase 1 evidence (2026-11-01): support matrix completes AV-001; XISF network tests complete AV-003. AV-002 is partial: 60 committed independent fixtures, 46 reverse-reader checks, and independent hashes for all 79 images in the 73-file local XISF corpus are implemented. The following substeps retain the original completion criteria: [x] AV-002.1: Redistributable FITS images, tables and independent TAN reference coordinates. [x] AV-002.2: Independent XISF codec/type/mono/RGB and attached/embedded fixtures, with exact pixels, provenance, hashes and licenses; independent checks of writer output. [x] AV-002.3: Local real photographs, multiple images, legacy astrometry metadata preservation and incomplete-thumbnail negative cases, with repeatable tests. [ ] AV-002.4: Independent distributed XISF containers, XISF tables, UInt64/complex pixels and big-endian/interleaved storage, with known reference values and reverse-reader checks. [ ] AV-002.5: A real native Revision 1 AstrometricSolution:* solution, including distortion and independent coordinate reference values. The downloaded legacy PCL:AstrometricSolution:* files cannot validate this evaluator. See interoperability for provenance, exact coverage and required follow-up. Phase 2 — Build a consistent scientific image-access foundation [ ] AV-004 — Design shared typed image and pixel-access contracts. Support explicit axes, channels, layout, sample types, scaling and missing-value masks. Keep native FITS/XISF documents accessible so a common view does not discard metadata. Preserve existing APIs or provide a documented migration path. Done when: the same operation can consume either format without first converting the entire file or forcing all samples through double. [ ] AV-005 — Add exact typed FITS pixel reads. Expose stored and physical values explicitly, including unsigned offset conventions and integer boundaries. Define behaviour when arbitrary scaling cannot be represented exactly. Done when: UInt64 values above 2^53, signed integers, BLANK, floating-point special values and overflow policies have independent regression tests. Depends on: AV-004. [ ] AV-006 — Add metadata-only opening and source indexing. Inspect headers, HDUs/images, geometry and block locations without materializing every payload. Define source lifetime, ownership and behaviour if source files change. Done when: a large-file header scan uses bounded memory and selected content can be opened without loading unrelated HDUs/images. [ ] AV-007 — Add format detection and a convenient opening API. Detect content rather than relying solely on filename extensions. Offer native-document access alongside shared image access, with clear unsupported/corrupt-input diagnostics. Done when: FITS, monolithic/distributed XISF headers and supported transport wrappers are identified consistently, including misleading filenames. Depends on: AV-004, AV-006; extend detection as compression is implemented. Phase 3 — Support common compressed FITS images [ ] AV-008 — Integrate gzip-wrapped FITS (.fits.gz). Add automatic reading and explicit writing options; retain caller-stream ownership and resource limits. Done when: path/stream APIs handle independently compressed files, truncated input and decompression limits. Document sequential-access costs. [ ] AV-009 — Recognize tiled compressed-image HDUs. Interpret ZIMAGE, ZBITPIX, ZNAXIS, ZTILE and codec metadata instead of exposing compressed images only as generic tables. Preserve access to the original storage representation. Done when: compressed images appear in image discovery with correct geometry, and unsupported codecs are reported precisely. Depends on: AV-006. [ ] AV-010 — Implement Rice and GZIP tile decoding/encoding. Cover applicable GZIP variants, edge tiles, integer storage, floating-point quantization/dithering, and undefined-pixel handling. Separate lossless storage from explicitly lossy modes. Done when: independent compressed fixtures decode correctly and reference readers accept output; quantized modes have explicit accuracy contracts. Depends on: AV-009. [ ] AV-011 — Add HCOMPRESS and PLIO support. Implement supported lossless modes first and require explicit options for lossy modes. Done when: independent fixtures, malformed tiles and algorithm-specific parameter boundaries are covered, with documented supported modes. Depends on: AV-009, AV-010. Phase 4 — Make large-image work bounded and cancellable [ ] AV-012 — Add row, region, channel and cube-plane reads. Provide exact typed reads and caller-provided buffers through the shared access contract. Read uncompressed regions directly and use tile/subblock access where possible. Done when: small requests avoid unrelated payloads when storage permits; whole-codec-block decoding requirements are explicit rather than hidden. Depends on: AV-004–AV-006, AV-009 for tiled FITS. [ ] AV-013 — Add streaming writes and compression. Avoid retaining every raw/compressed attachment or complete output image in memory. Support chunked access beyond individual CLR-array limits where the format permits it. Done when: measured peak memory stays bounded as file size increases, while checksums, layout, metadata and failure guarantees remain correct. Depends on: AV-004, AV-006, AV-012. [ ] AV-014 — Add asynchronous I/O, decode cancellation and progress. Go beyond worker-thread wrappers; propagate cancellation through reads, codecs and writes at documented checkpoints. Keep progress reporting bounded. Done when: cancellation during expensive operations releases resources and preserves existing single-file output; non-interruptible stages are documented. Depends on: AV-003, AV-012, AV-013. [ ] AV-015 — Complete the document lifetime and safe-save model. Provide an explicit fully detached/materialized document operation. Design distributed-XISF staging, recovery and replacement behaviour without promising impossible atomic replacement of two independent files. Done when: deleting the original after detachment cannot break a later save, and failure/cancellation tests cover each distributed publication stage. Depends on: AV-006, AV-013. Phase 5 — Complete table editing and cross-format fidelity [ ] AV-016 — Add typed FITS table builders and editable serialization. Create and edit ASCII/binary columns and rows, fixed arrays and variable-length heaps. Serialize the edited model rather than requiring callers to construct raw bytes. Done when: create/edit/save/reload tests cover values, units, scaling, nulls, extension metadata, checksums and existing resource budgets. [ ] AV-017 — Complete table shape, null and precision semantics. Interpret TDIM, preserve logical NULL independently of false, and support exact unsigned integer column access where scaling is exactly representable. Done when: independent catalog fixtures cover multidimensional columns, nullable logical values and UInt64 boundaries without hidden precision loss. Depends on: AV-016. [ ] AV-018 — Define preservation-aware document conversion. Specify mappings for tables, array cells, units, global/image properties, extensions, ancillary metadata and astrometry. Use documented preservation extensions where appropriate. Done when: each feature has an explicit preserved/transformed/omitted result; lossy conversion still requires opt-in. Do not promise universal losslessness: standard FITS image HDUs cannot directly represent XISF complex pixels, and not every XISF property/XML structure has a standard FITS counterpart. Depends on: AV-001, AV-004, AV-016, AV-017. Phase 6 — Broaden astrometry [ ] AV-019 — Support common FITS SIP/TPV distortions. Evaluate forward and inverse transformations with explicit convergence and precision policies. Done when: independent real solutions and reference calculations agree across image centres, edges and difficult inverse cases; unsupported variants fail clearly. [ ] AV-020 — Extend FITS projection and coordinate conventions. Add projections by demonstrated need, axis ordering, angular units, alternate WCS solutions and supported pole parameters. Keep reference-frame conversion explicit. Done when: every advertised convention has independent reference values, domain-boundary tests and documented units/origins. Depends on: AV-019. [ ] AV-021 — Add spectral/time-axis and reference-frame capabilities. Define supported spectral quantities, time scales and celestial frame transformations as separate capabilities. Add table WCS when extending catalog workflows. Done when: supported standards/conventions, required metadata, precision and unsupported cases are explicit and independently tested. Depends on: AV-020; prioritize optical imaging before specialist workflows. [ ] AV-022 — Bridge native XISF and FITS astrometry where representable. Keep their distinct pixel origins and distortion models explicit; never substitute an approximate transform silently during conversion. Done when: supported conversions have coordinate-error bounds and report unrepresentable models without discarding the original solution. Depends on: AV-018–AV-020. Phase 7 — Add shared image-processing features These are useful application capabilities, not requirements for reading either format. [ ] AV-023 — Add geometry-aware crop, rotation, resize and reprojection. Update geometry, WCS/native astrometry, CFA and ancillary metadata consistently. Done when: known sky/pixel correspondences remain valid or incompatible metadata is explicitly removed with a diagnostic; scientific pixels remain owned. Depends on: AV-004, AV-012, AV-019–AV-022 as applicable. [ ] AV-024 — Add CFA debayering. Interpret native/FITS CFA metadata and offsets; define initial algorithms, edge handling and output sample precision. Done when: independent mosaics verify orientation, offsets, colour channels, source preservation and metadata updates for both formats. Depends on: AV-004, AV-023 metadata rules. [ ] AV-025 — Extend analysis to cubes and complex data. Add plane/spectrum selection and explicit real/imaginary/magnitude/phase views rather than treating arbitrary axes as colour channels. Done when: shared operations handle these views with correct axes, units, sample precision and missing values. Depends on: AV-004, AV-012, AV-021 where physical axes are evaluated. [ ] AV-026 — Define later scientific-processing modules. Scope calibration, registration, stacking, photometry and plate solving individually before implementing them. Separate display enhancements from scientific measurements. Done when: each selected module has accuracy requirements, provenance rules, independent validation datasets and a focused follow-up checklist. Depends on: shared image access and the relevant geometry/astrometry capabilities. Phase 8 — Profile and fill specialist coverage [ ] AV-027 — Benchmark remaining allocation hotspots. Measure table-cell boxing, matrix decoding, rectangular-array factories, typed row copies and per-pixel Lab transforms before specializing them. Done when: reproducible before/after throughput and allocation results show a benefit without weakening precision, ownership, checksums or readability. Can proceed alongside earlier phases when real workloads identify a bottleneck. [ ] AV-028 — Add specialist FITS capabilities by demand. Assess random-groups/ UVFITS, compressed tables and other survey/radio conventions separately from common optical-image support. Done when: chosen features appear in the support matrix with independent fixtures and explicit read/write/edit/preservation guarantees. Depends on: AV-001; defer until common image/table workflows are dependable. Completion rules for every implementation step Preserve existing public contracts or document intentional compatibility changes. Include independent fixtures or reference values as well as round-trip tests. Test corrupt/truncated data, resource limits, precision boundaries and cancellation relevant to the change. Do not use machine-dependent performance assertions. Run relevant checks and Windows/Linux/macOS CI; keep large/private datasets outside Git. Update the support matrix, usage documentation and this checklist with evidence. Primary references: FITS 4.0, FITS WCS, FITS tile compression, XISF specification.

support-matrix.html.title: FITS/XISF support matrix | AstroView documentation
support-matrix.html.summary: FITS/XISF support matrix Baseline updated against the source, regression tests and independent fixtures on 2026-11-01. This is an implementation contract and gap inventory, not certification of full FITS 4.0 or XISF Revision 1 conformance. Update the matrix with each release and link new independent interoperability evidence as it becomes available. How to read the matrix Yes: the documented API implements the capability for the stated scope. Partial: a restriction or preservation condition in the notes matters. No: the capability is not implemented as a supported high-level operation. —: not applicable to that feature. The columns are deliberately independent: Read means expose the content as a supported model, not merely retain bytes. Write means serialize supported content; raw-payload passthrough is identified. Edit means change the supported model and save it using public APIs. Replacing a complete image is different from a random-access or in-place file edit. Preserve means retain the stated information through the relevant save path. It does not promise byte-identical files, preservation of arbitrary unknown content in every editing path, or lossless conversion between formats. Evaluate means interpret the feature's semantics, such as physical sample scaling, integrity verification or a coordinate transform. Keeping a WCS header does not mean its transform can be evaluated. Classes of features: Format covers native format structures/semantics; Convention covers a particular FITS/application convention; API covers access, editing or workflow behaviour; Processing covers image/astronomy work above file-format I/O. A missing processing operation is not missing format decoding. FITS containers, pixels and headers Feature / class Read Write Edit Preserve Evaluate Scope and evidence Primary image and IMAGE extension HDUs; multiple HDUs — Format Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Public models support complete image replacement. Geometry and payload bytes are retained; records/cards are reserialized. Models, tests. Standard BITPIX image storage: 8, 16, 32, 64, -32, -64 — Format Yes Yes Yes Yes Partial Raw storage is available. GetPhysicalSamples() returns doubles, so not every large integer is exactly representable in that view. Samples, independent-byte tests. BSCALE/BZERO, integer BLANK and standard unsigned image offsets — Format/convention Yes Yes Yes Yes Partial Physical doubles apply scaling and map integer BLANK to NaN. Exact unsigned conversion paths exist in FitsConverter; arbitrary scaling can round and inexact signed-64 conversion is rejected. Converter, boundary tests, conversion tests. Scientific N-dimensional image storage — Format Yes Yes Yes Yes Partial Axis lengths remain scientific dimensions unless RGB/RGBA interpretation is explicitly requested. No general cube-plane/physical-axis processing API. axis tests. Header values, ordered/repeated COMMENT and HISTORY — Format Yes Yes Yes Partial Yes Typed/custom keyword access is supported. Structural image cards are guarded and regenerated with the payload. Header order/formatting is not a byte-copy guarantee. Header, metadata tests. HIERARCH and long strings with CONTINUE — Convention Yes Yes Yes Partial Yes Strings, escaped apostrophes and final continuation comments are handled. Writer rejects non-printable/non-ASCII or overlong cards instead of silently truncating semantic content. Writer, regressions. CHECKSUM/DATASUM — Convention Yes Yes — Partial Yes Writer can recompute checksums; reader reports nullable results when missing. Re-encoding changes serialized checksums. Checksum, tests. Unknown extension payloads — Format/API Partial Partial Partial Partial No Opaque HDU payloads can be retained/replaced and re-emitted. Their application semantics are not decoded, and cross-format conversion may omit them. HDU model, tests. Gzip-wrapped .fits.gz — Transport/API No No No No — No integrated detection/wrapper. A caller can provide a decompression stream to the ordinary FITS reader. Path/stream entry points. Planned AV-008. Tiled compressed images / .fits.fz — Format/convention No No No Partial No No ZIMAGE/ZCMPTYPE image interpretation or tile codecs. Generic table/raw storage may survive a FITS save; this is not compressed-image support. HDU dispatch. Planned AV-009–AV-011. Random groups / radio UVFITS — Format/convention No No No No No Some enum/length recognition exists, but there is no supported random-groups document/data model. Reader, document validation. Planned AV-028. FITS tables Feature / class Read Write Edit Preserve Evaluate Scope and evidence ASCII tables — Format Yes Partial Partial Partial Partial Decoded rows are read-only. Existing tables can be saved from retained raw storage; there is no typed table builder or serialization of edited decoded rows. Unscaled I fields retain Int64; scaled numeric fields use double. Reader, tests. Binary scalar/fixed-array fields, bit/complex/logical fields — Format Partial Partial Partial Partial Partial Supported type codes decode; typed vectors are exposed. Logical missing-value handling is incomplete, and scaled integer values may lose precision through double. Writing/editing requires retained or manually rebuilt raw storage. Reader, tests. P/Q variable-length heap arrays — Format Yes Partial Partial Partial Yes Zero/one descriptor repetition, empty arrays, bounds and decoded-element budgets are checked. No public typed heap builder. Reader, boundary tests. Table TSCAL/TZERO/TNULL and units — Format Partial Partial Partial Partial Partial Metadata and supported null/scaling semantics are decoded. ASCII null text is recognized before conversion. Exact unsigned-64 scaled columns and logical null semantics need further work. Column model, tests. Multidimensional columns / TDIM — Format Partial Partial No Partial No The keyword can be read/preserved through the header, but decoded array fields remain flat and TDIM shape semantics are not evaluated. Keyword catalog, table parser. Planned AV-017. Compressed tables — Format/convention No No No Partial No No decompression/editing API; opaque supported storage may be retained as a generic table. Table dispatch. Planned AV-028. XISF containers, samples and metadata Feature / class Read Write Edit Preserve Evaluate Scope and evidence Monolithic XISF; distributed XISH + indexed XISB — Format Yes Yes Yes Partial Yes Distributed output is two sequential files, not a transaction. Original sources may remain necessary for opaque blocks. Writer, container tests, path tests. Attached, embedded and inline Base64/hex data; both byte orders — Format Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Size limits apply before text decoding/allocation. Editing is through owned models, not arbitrary in-place updates. Blocks, storage tests, resource tests. zlib, LZ4, LZ4HC, Zstandard; shuffle/subblocks/alignment — Format Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Codecs process full blocks/subblocks; region access does not imply partial decompression. Reader, writer, codec matrix tests. SHA-1, SHA-256/512, SHA3-256/512 block digests — Format Yes Yes — Partial Yes Digests verify serialized bytes before decompression. Lazy blocks are not verified merely by reading the XML header; re-encoding computes new digests. Blocks, SHA-3 tests. UInt8/16/32/64, Float32/64, Complex32/64 image samples — Format Yes Yes Yes Yes Partial Exact matching-type sample paths exist. Complex values can be read, but the ordinary display/statistics/region helpers do not process complex images. Image, editable image, numeric tests. Arbitrary axes; planar/interleaved channels; Gray/RGB/CIELab — Format Yes Yes Yes Yes Partial Storage is supported; built-in rendering, regions, statistics and histograms are mainly 2D real-image APIs. Utilities, layout tests. Scalar properties, vectors/matrices, Boolean/String/TimePoint — Format Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Typed and custom identifiers; case-sensitive property access. Known-field/property editing is distinct from preserving arbitrary unknown XML. Properties, type tests, catalog tests. 128-bit integer and binary128 real/complex property storage — Format Yes Yes Yes Yes Partial Precise storage/parsing/formatting is supported; these types are not a general quadruple-precision arithmetic or image-pixel engine. Types, tests. XISF document/image tables, including array cells — Format Yes Yes Yes Partial Yes Editable fields/rows are supported. Unknown/unavailable cells may retain source-backed opaque representations. Table models, document editing, tests. FITS keywords, ICC, thumbnail, CFA, RGB working space, display function, resolution and orientation — Format Yes Yes Yes Partial Partial Color/display transforms are implemented. CFA is metadata, not debayering; ICC data is retained, not a full ICC colour-management engine. Orientation affects previews, not automatically scientific storage. Models, renderer, tests. Unknown extensions/types and unavailable optional objects — Format/API Partial Partial Partial Partial No Preserve through document-aware save paths without interpreting unsupported semantics. Rebuilding an editable image does not guarantee arbitrary unknown attributes survive. Editable document, preservation tests. Detached XML signatures — Format Yes Partial Partial Partial Partial RSA signing and embedded-key integrity checks are implemented. An edit/layout change generally requires re-signing. Verification does not establish signer identity, certificate-chain trust or arbitrary XML-subset transform support. Signing, tests. Header-relative/external resources and URL resolution — Format/API Partial Yes Partial Partial Partial Filesystem/network access follows explicit policies; network access is disabled by default. Custom resolvers are optional. HTTP acquisition/body reads honor NetworkTimeout; custom resolvers/streams must cooperate. See timeout tests. Options, blocks, policy tests. Semantic and caller-supplied XSD validation — Format/API Yes — — — Partial Diagnostics and Validate(XmlSchemaSet) exist. The library does not ship an exhaustive certification oracle or imply that loading a header verifies every lazy payload. Validation, API, tests. Coordinates and astronomical semantics Feature / class Read Write Edit Preserve Evaluate Scope and evidence FITS WCS keywords as header metadata — Format/convention Yes Yes Yes Yes Partial Reading/preserving CTYPE, distortion or alternate-WCS cards does not imply their transform is supported. Typed keys, metadata tests. Degree-based RA/DEC TAN, CD or PC/CDELT — Format/convention Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes The convenience evaluator supports this axis order and its documented pole/default restrictions. Headers without both CTYPE values retain a legacy linear mode. WCS evaluator, tests. FITS SIP/TPV, other projections, alternate/axis-swapped/non-degree WCS, spectral/time/table WCS — Convention/Format Yes Yes Yes Yes No Metadata remains accessible; unsupported explicit transforms are rejected rather than approximated. Coordinate-frame transformations are also not implemented. WCS gate, rejection tests. Planned AV-019–AV-022. Native XISF Revision 1 astrometry — Format Yes Yes Partial Partial Yes Seven projections, spherical rotation, both stored projective directions, spline distortion layers and fallback are implemented. Known properties can be edited, but the library does not fit/solve the models. Evaluator, projection/distortion tests. Future/unknown native astrometric revisions — Format/API Partial Partial No Partial No Retain unavailable representations through preserving save paths; do not claim evaluation of unknown revisions. Evaluator, preservation tests. Common object/instrument/observation metadata — API Yes Yes Yes Partial Partial A normalized view exposes selected known fields; it is not a complete physical-unit/time-scale conversion system. Metadata, quote/case tests. Access, interchange and image work Feature / class Read Write Edit Preserve Evaluate Scope and evidence Full FITS↔XISF image conversion with findings — API Yes Yes Partial Partial Partial Images/selected metadata convert; tables/global properties/ancillary objects may be transformed or omitted. Losses reject by default. No universal losslessness: complex XISF pixels have no standard FITS image-HDU equivalent. Converter, loss tests. Shared format-neutral scientific image facade — API No No No — No Existing image utilities are principally XISF-oriented. FITS users can convert or use native models. Planned AV-004–AV-007. Metadata-only/selective opening — API Partial — — — — XISF path opening keeps image blocks lazy; FITS materializes all HDU payloads. No general shared header-only/index API. FITS reader, XISF reader. Region/channel access — API Partial No No — Partial XISF 2D real-image helpers return selected data after reading/decompressing the complete source block. No native FITS ROI/cube-plane or bounded-memory shared interface. Utilities, tests. Unbounded-size/chunked image storage and streaming compression — API No No — — — Current data models use whole arrays/int-sized blocks and intermediate compression buffers. Defaults impose additional limits; raising them does not remove CLR-array ceilings. Options, writer blocks. Async APIs, cancellation and progress — API Partial Partial — — — Worker-thread wrappers with cooperative checkpoints exist; this is not fully async I/O, cancellable lazy decode, or general progress reporting. Async writer, ownership/cancellation tests. Atomic single-file path save — API — Yes Yes Yes — Stage then replace on success; caller streams and distributed two-file saves have different guarantees. Helper, failure tests. Explicit full document detachment/safe distributed publication — API Partial Partial Partial Partial — Materializing editable pixels may leave opaque metadata source-backed. Two files cannot be assumed to publish atomically. Editable document contract. Planned AV-015. 2D real-image statistics, histograms and display stretching/rendering — Processing Yes Partial No Yes Yes Utilities return derived values/BGRA previews without modifying scientific samples. Preview pixels can be consumed by an application; no general raster-file encoder is included. Utilities, renderer tests, numeric tests. Geometry-aware scientific crop/rotate/resize/reprojection — Processing No No No No No Reading a region or orienting a preview is not an editing pipeline that updates WCS, CFA and ancillary metadata. Planned AV-023. CFA debayering, cube/complex analysis views — Processing No No No — No These data/metadata can be stored, but equivalent shared processing operations are absent. Planned AV-024–AV-025. Calibration, registration, stacking, photometry and plate solving — Processing No No No — No No claims are made merely because image pixels and astrometric solutions can be loaded. Planned AV-026. Evidence and interpretation limits Source/test links identify the implementation and representative regressions, not exhaustive proof of all combinations. Existing generated-byte, round-trip, malformed input and cross-platform tests are complemented by Phase 1 independent-reader fixtures; the fixture provenance/manifests must distinguish independently produced files from files produced by AstroView for reverse-direction checks. The optional local corpus test checks user photographs outside Git. Eleven FITS photographs passed the previous review. The local XISF test now checks independent pixel hashes for 73 files/79 images, metadata/attachment preservation for complete files and two known missing-thumbnail failures. Sixty small committed independent fixtures run on all three CI platforms. Real native XISF distortion solutions still need independent reference evidence before broad interoperability claims are made. Keep external fixture redistribution licenses and source hashes alongside the fixtures. Use the roadmap to select the next gap, and testing for commands and the distinction between portable fixtures and local photographs. Format references: FITS 4.0, FITS WCS, FITS tile compression, XISF specification. Phase 1 evidence: independent corpus and limitations, offline fixture tests. The desktop workspace exposes the currently implemented capabilities through a feature guide and interactive tools. Its demonstration files are not independent producer fixtures. GUI integration also protects the optional absence of an ordered interval for complex samples: bounds validation regressions.

testing.html.title: Testing FITS and XISF | AstroView documentation
testing.html.summary: Testing FITS and XISF The solution also includes desktop workflow and rendering checks for the Avalonia application. They run headlessly on all three CI platforms and keep GUI dependencies out of the Core project. Large desktop corpus checks are separately opt-in with ASTROVIEW_DESKTOP_EXAMPLES. Portable regression suite dotnet restore AstroView.sln --locked-mode dotnet build AstroView.sln -c Release --no-restore dotnet test AstroView.sln -c Release --no-build --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage" CI runs the same suite and package build on Windows, Linux, and macOS. Generated fixtures require no network or photograph corpus. Tests exercise: Independent FITS/XISF bytes, truncated headers/payloads/padding, invalid UTF-8, malformed text encodings, unsupported headers, DTD rejection, and resource limits. FITS empty HDUs, zero-sized axes, floating-point special values, big-endian storage, scaling, integer BLANK, unsigned boundaries, and variable-array heap bounds. Every XISF codec/checksum combination in both byte orders, shuffle/subblock tails, planar/interleaved channels, and deliberate payload corruption before decompression. One-byte and short reads through seekable/non-seekable streams, sync/async APIs, exact buffering limits, stream ownership, Unicode filenames, atomic replacement, and invariant parsing under German, French, and Turkish cultures. Existing metadata, conversion, rendering, cancellation, and signature regressions. These checks establish behaviour on the tested runners, not universal support for all operating systems, architectures, or file variants. Tests do not contact external URLs. The local corpus is not uploaded to GitHub. Local example corpus The corpus test is explicitly skipped unless ASTROVIEW_EXAMPLES is set. A configured missing/empty directory fails rather than silently passing. Run it separately because the photographs can require hundreds of MB per document: $env:ASTROVIEW_EXAMPLES = 'C:\Code\AstroExamples' $env:ASTROVIEW_EXAMPLE_REPORT = "$PWD\artifacts\local-examples\report.json" $env:ASTROVIEW_XISF_EXAMPLE_REPORT = "$PWD\artifacts\local-examples\xisf-report.json" dotnet test AstroView.sln -c Release --filter Category=LocalExamples Remove-Item Env:ASTROVIEW_EXAMPLES Remove-Item Env:ASTROVIEW_EXAMPLE_REPORT Remove-Item Env:ASTROVIEW_XISF_EXAMPLE_REPORT On Linux/macOS use ASTROVIEW_EXAMPLES=/path/to/images dotnet test AstroView.sln -c Release --filter Category=LocalExamples (on one line). The report path is optional. Reports belong under ignored artifacts/. The local test recursively checks .fits, .fit, and .fts files, one at a time, without modifying them. It independently scans physical header cards to compare image axes and BITPIX, checks the payload sizes, compares SHA-256 of every loaded payload byte against the original file, verifies present checksums, and requires no error-level diagnostics or unread trailing bytes. Missing checksums are accepted and do not establish integrity. The report records filenames, lengths, payload hashes, failures, OS, runtime, and process architecture. This validates loading/storage fidelity, not image aesthetics or independently calibrated pixel/astrometric correctness. The supplied corpus currently contains 11 FITS files plus 73 downloaded XISF files containing 79 primary images. The XISF test checks the committed Fixtures/LocalXisf/manifest.json against files in the XISF subdirectory (or the configured directory itself). Every listed file must exist and match its original SHA-256. Independent reference hashes come from the pinned Python reader or the separately identified base64/zlib oracle. The test checks pixels/geometry/layout/types, then saves/reloads the 71 complete files in a temporary directory and compares all pixels and preserved XML metadata. Two sources have missing thumbnail attachments: their primary pixels are checked, but thumbnail access and complete saving must fail. Source files are never edited. Set ASTROVIEW_XISF_EXAMPLE_REPORT to record per-file results and semantic diagnostics separately from the FITS report. Successful pixel decoding does not require these legacy producer files to pass strict semantic validation. The large local corpus has been exercised on Windows; the 60 small committed independent fixtures run on Windows/Linux/macOS CI. No external images enter the package. Review and performance measurements See the code review for resolved findings, compatibility changes, remaining limitations, and the median/MAD benchmark. Run the benchmark with dotnet run --project tools/AstroView.Performance -c Release. It checks result equivalence and reports timing/allocation measurements; CI does not assert machine-dependent timing thresholds.

versioning.html.title: Versioning and releases | AstroView documentation
versioning.html.summary: Versioning and releases AstroView uses Semantic Versioning. The next release version is defined once in eng/Versions.props; this implementation advances it from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0. While the major version is zero, minor releases can include documented API changes. Patch releases are reserved for compatible corrections. Record changes in CHANGELOG.md. Build Package version Local/default 0.2.0-dev CI push or pull request 0.2.0-ci.<run-number>.<attempt> Tag v0.2.0-rc.1 0.2.0-rc.1 Tag v0.2.0 0.2.0 Assembly/file versions use the numeric release prefix (0.2.0.0). Informational versions retain the package version and SDK-provided Git commit metadata for traceability. A tag must match the configured version; CI rejects mismatches and invalid prerelease identifiers. Build metadata belongs in the informational version, not the release tag. CI reruns receive distinct prerelease package versions. Building a version explicitly dotnet build AstroView.sln -c Release -p:Version=0.2.0-rc.1 dotnet test AstroView.sln -c Release --no-build dotnet pack src/AstroView.Core/AstroView.Core.csproj -c Release --no-build -p:Version=0.2.0-rc.1 -o artifacts/packages Build and pack must use the same version. CI resolves it once with eng/Get-BuildVersion.ps1 and reuses it throughout the workflow. Run eng/Test-BuildVersion.ps1 in PowerShell to check the policy. Release checklist Update eng/Versions.props and the changelog; review intentional API changes. Restore locked dependencies; build, test, and pack on supported CI platforms. Verify the package version, assembly version, informational commit metadata, dependency list, README, and attribution files. Create and push the matching v<version> tag when a release is authorized. The release workflow validates, tests and publishes a GitHub Release with separate desktop and Core archives. It does not publish to NuGet. Advance the prefix for subsequent development; do not move an already published tag. No release tag or public package is created merely by changing this version file.
